It is advisable to split curved Surfaces using Lines that are manifolded over the Surface. In the example shown here, the original Surface is split at Line 5. Points 5 and 6, defining Line 5, must lie on the original Surface boundary Lines.

headings: Split surface by single point (Insert menu) (Geometry Menu)
topics.text: Split surface by single point (Insert menu) (Geometry Menu) Splits a selected Surface at a single Point defined on the surface inside the boundary. Four new Surfaces are created by manifolding straight Lines or arcs onto the existing Surface using the relative position of the splitting Point. In this example, the original Surface is split at Point 5. The resulting Surfaces (2-5), use parametric space to calculate boundary Point positions.

The Surfaces can snap to grid at a predefined Z plane. This command is only available when viewing the XY plane. Tip. topics.text: Surface by coordinates (Geometry Menu) Defines a general, cylindrical, conical or spherical Surface by entering a list of X, Y and Z coordinates (Z is optional). If a non - Cartesian local coordinate system is in use the coordinates are specified in the coordinate system of that local coordinate set. Coordinates can be entered using global (default) and local coordinate systems. Shortcuts Drop tool (Smart Surface)

toc_path: Surface by joining sets of Lines (Geometry Menu)
headings: Surface by joining sets of Lines (Geometry Menu)
topics.text: Surface by joining sets of Lines (Geometry Menu) Defines a number of Surfaces by joining two sets of selected Lines. The first set of Lines should be added to memory, the second set should be selected with the cursor. The Lines should pair up equally. Surfaces are joined according to the order in which the Lines were selected, i.e. first Line in memory joins to first Line selected with cursor ,etc. In the example shown Surfaces 1 and 2 are defined by first selecting Lines 1 and 2 then adding them to memory , then selecting Lines 3 and 4 and using the Surface by joining command. Shortcuts Drop tool (Smart Surface)

topics.title: Surface by Lines (Geometry Menu)
topics.text: Surface by Lines (Geometry Menu) Defines a Surface from three or more selected Lines. When defining Surfaces in this way, any number of Lines may be specified in any order and a Surface will be formed from the greatest number of lines that form a closed loop. LUSAS will filter out duplicated Lines and any unconnected Lines. If defining a bicubic patch the boundary lines must be given first, followed by the internal lines. Shortcuts Drop tool (Smart Surface)

topics.title: Tangent between two arcs (Geometry Menu)
topics.text: Tangent between two arcs (Geometry Menu) Defines a Line which is tangent to two coplanar Arcs. The new Line can be defined as an inside or outside tangent. Options are available to split the Arcs at the new Points, and then delete the original Arcs. In this example Line 3 is created as an outside tangent to Lines 1 and 2.

topics.title: Arc tangent to 2 Lines (Geometry Menu)
topics.text: Arc tangent to 2 Lines (Geometry Menu) Defines an Arc tangent to two selected Lines, either major Arc or minor Arc. The tangent lines must be straight Lines or Arcs. Options are available to split the original Lines at the point of contact, then delete the original Lines. In this example Line 3 is defined by selecting Lines 1 and 2, specifying a radius and choosing the minor Arc option. Alternatively, Line 4 (shown as a dotted line for clarity) would be defined if the major Arc option were chosen.

toc_path: Tangent between point and arc (Geometry Menu)
headings: Tangent between point and arc (Geometry Menu)
topics.text: Tangent between point and arc (Geometry Menu) Defines a Line between a selected Point and the tangent to a selected Arc. This command cannot be used if there is no tangent possible, or if there are 2 possible tangents. Options are available to split the Arc at the new Point, and then delete the original Arc. In this example Line 2 is created by specifying Line 1 and Point 4. Point 5 is automatically created.

headings: Spline tangent to two Lines (Geometry Menu)
topics.text: Spline tangent to two Lines (Geometry Menu) Defines a Spline passing through two or more selected Points. The Spline end vectors are taken from the directions of two selected Lines. topics.title: 1. Volume by joining selected features
topics.text: 1. Volume by joining selected features Joins two selected features to form a Volume, either a Point to a Surface, or a Line to a Surface, or two Surfaces. The features are joined by straight lines. Surface 1 is joined to Point 4 to form a pentahedral. Surface 1 defines the local xy axes of the Volume. Surface 1 joined to Line 5. Volume x axis defined from one triangular Surface to the other. Local y axis runs along the first Line of Surface 1. Surface 1 is joined to Surface 2 to form a hexahedral. Two triangular Surfaces joined this way would form a pentahedral. 2. Volume by joining Surfaces in pairs Defines groups of Volumes by joining two sets of selected Surfaces. The first set of Surfaces should be added to memory (Edit menu), the second set should be selected with the cursor. The Surfaces should pair up equally. Volumes are joined according to the order in which the Surfaces were selected, i.e. first Surfaces in memory joins to first Surfaces selected with cursor ,etc. Shortcuts Drop tool (Smart Volume)

headings: Design Code selection and combination options
topics.text: Design Code selection and combination options After selecting a country's design code, each loadcase that is to be used in the design combination should be assigned a pre-defined load type prior to accessing the combination options page of the design combination wizard. Multiple assignments of the same loadtype can be assigned by selecting the first occurence of the loadcase name, holding-down the Shift key, and then clicking in the load Type cell of the last occurence of the loadcase name to be assigned the same load type. The load type for all selections can then be selected from the drop-down list of those available. Note that envelopes and basic combinations can be assigned a load type, but smart combinations cannot. Combination options relating to the selected design code also need to be specified. An option to choose the combination approach using either basic or smart combinations can be selected. Note that the load factors are included in the combination name for a basic combination but this is not done for a smart combination due to the variable nature of the factors. An envelope can also be optionally created for each combination type. Representative design combination wizard page 1 Representative design combination wizard page 2 Where design combinations are to be used along with design code checking facilities, such as Steel Frame Design Steel Frame Design , RC Frame design RC Frame design or RC slab/wall design RC slab/wall design it is recommended that basic combinations are used. topics.search_text: Design Code selection and combination options Design Combinations Application Manual (Bridge, Civil and Structural) Design Combinations Overview Design Code selection and combination options Design idh design combinations.htm Design Code selection and combination options After selecting a country's design code, each loadcase that is to be used in the design combination should be assigned a pre-defined load type prior to accessing the combination options page of the design combination wizard. Multiple assignments of the same loadtype can be assigned by selecting the first occurence of the loadcase name, holding-down the Shift key, and then clicking in the load Type cell of the last occurence of the loadcase name to be assigned the same load type. The load type for all selections can then be selected from the drop-down list of those available. Note that envelopes and basic combinations can be assigned a load type, but smart combinations cannot. Combination options relating to the selected design code also need to be specified. An option to choose the combination approach using either basic or smart combinations can be selected. Note that the load factors are included in the combination name for a basic combination but this is not done for a smart combination due to the variable nature of the factors. An envelope can also be optionally created for each combination type. topics.title: Advanced options
topics.text: Advanced options The Advanced options dialog provides an editable listing of the load types and the associated factors to be considered. Load types are separated into Permanent actions and Variable actions. Factors for table entries can be edited. Load types can also be set to be mutually exclusive, or not. When mutually exclusive is set to 'Yes' loadcases that have the same load type assigned are accommodated, but these loadcases are not included in a combination simultaneously.

topics.title: On completion
topics.text: On completion On completion, separate Design Combination parent folders are created for Basic and Smart Combinations in the Analyses Treeview, containing folders holding (using the Eurocode as an example) the SLS Characteristic, SLS Frequent, SLS Quasi-permanent, and ULS Persistent (Eq 6.10) load combinations. A Max and Min envelope of the relevant loads may also be created inside each combination folder if this option is selected. In the case of a smart combination a Constituents folder is also created if there are load types that are to be considered at the same time.

topics.title: Viewing results
topics.text: Viewing results Results are always visualised for the active loadcase. To make a loadcase active, right - click on the loadcase in the Analyses Treeview, and choose Set Active from the context menu. See Visualising the results from Combinations and Envelopes Visualising the results from Combinations and Envelopes for general notes regarding viewing results. Notes The design combination wizard is particularly intended for use with results output from the LUSAS Vehicle Load Optimisation LUSAS Vehicle Load Optimisation facility. For the bridge design codes supported by LUSAS Vehcile Load Optimisation, suitable loadcases can be created with appropriate lane factors and loading arrangement and an appropriate load type can be assigned to each loadcase. Depending upon the loading code used the load factor may be applied in the Vehicle Load Optimisation facility, negating the need to apply a factor in the Design combination wizard. As an example, in the case of the Eurocode, loadcases would need to be created for the characteristic, combination, frequent and quasi permanent combinations with the ψ factors applied to them in the VLO facility but the load factor  Q is not assigned. When using envelopes it should be noted that the maximum and minimum envelopes will generally not be grouped together

topics.title: Shear and torsion checks
toc_path: RC Frame Tabulated Results and Calculations
Implementation Notes for RC Frame Design Checks to AASHTO 8th and 9th Edition
headings: Implementation Notes for RC Frame Design Checks to AASHTO 8th and 9th Edition
topics.text: Shear and torsion checks Shear and torsion checks are carried out for reinforced concrete sections (excluding prestressing) to Article 5.7. The implementation does not currently include principal tensile stresses in webs (5.9.2.3.3) because this would apply to post-tensioned and pretensioned members only, or to interface shear (5.7.4) Shear and torsion checks only support design for B-regions (beam or Bernoulli) with reference to 5.5.1.2 of the code. Design for D-regions (distributed regions such as those near supports and the points of application of concentrated load) is not currently supported. Design checks are applied to members that are defined using: 3-dimensional beam line meshes (thick beam, thick cross section beam, thick beam with torsional warping, thick cross section beam with torsional warping, thin beam, semiloof beam, semiloof cross section beam). In members that are tapered along their length, the components of inclined tension or compression forces are not taken into account in the calculation of shear strength. Maximum transverse shear near a support is not reduced. Additional longitudinal forces are not included in longitudinal reinforcement. The calculation algorithms are only applicable for beams under shear in one direction. If shear forces occur in two directions within a section, separate checks will have to be carried out for each direction.

topics.text: Shear and torsion checks Shear and torsion checks are carried out for reinforced concrete sections (excluding prestressing) in accordance with clause 8.9. Design checks are applied to members that are defined using: 3-dimensional beam line meshes (thick beam, thick cross section beam, thick beam with torsional warping, thick cross section beam with torsional warping, thin beam, semiloof beam, semiloof cross section beam). In members that are tapered along their length, the components of inclined tension or compression forces are not taken into account in the calculation of shear strength. Maximum transverse shear near a support is not reduced. Additional longitudinal forces are not included in longitudinal reinforcement. The calculation algorithms are only applicable for beams under shear in one direction. This means that considered beam can only have sets of loads of My, Mz, Fx, Fz, Mx (Fy - negligible small values) and My, Mz, Fx, Fy, Mx (Fz - negligible small values) If shear forces occur in two directions within a section, separate checks will have to be carried out for each direction. Implementation does not include deflection limits check 9.3.2 and 24.2

topics.text: Shear and torsion Shear and torsion checks are carried out for reinforced concrete sections (excluding prestressing) according to AS 5100.5:2017 clause 8.2. The implementation does not allow for prestressing. There is no guidance in the design code of what to do when there are shear forces in two directions in a section. The user has the option to carry out two independent checks: shear in y direction and shear in z direction. Design checks are applied to members that are defined using: 3-dimensional beam line meshes (thick beam, thick cross section beam, thick beam with torsional warping, thick cross section beam with torsional warping, thin beam, semiloof beam, semiloof cross section beam). In members that are tapered along their length, the components of inclined tension or compression forces are not taken into account in the calculation of shear strength. Maximum transverse shear near a support is not reduced. Additional longitudinal forces are not included in longitudinal reinforcement. The calculation algorithms are only applicable for beams under shear in one direction. If shear forces occur in two directions within a section, separate checks will have to be carried out for each direction. This means that a beam can only have the following sets of loads of My, Mz, Fx, Fz, Mx (Fy - negligible small values) or My, Mz, Fx, Fz, Mx (Fy - negligible small values).

headings: Implementation Notes for RC Frame Design Checks to CSA S6-14 and CSA S6:19
topics.text: Shear and torsion notes Shear and torsion checks are carried out for reinforced concrete sections (excluding prestressing) in accordance with Clause 8.9 There is no guidance in the design code of what to do when there are shear forces in two directions in a section. The user has the option to carry out two independent checks: shear in y direction and shear in z direction. Design checks are applied to members that are defined using: 3-dimensional beam line meshes (thick beam, thick cross section beam, thick beam with torsional warping, thick cross section beam with torsional warping, thin beam, semiloof beam, semiloof cross section beam). In members that are tapered along their length, the components of inclined tension or compression forces are not taken into account in the calculation of shear strength. Maximum transverse shear near a support is not reduced. Additional longitudinal forces are not included in longitudinal reinforcement. The calculation algorithms are only applicable for beams under shear in one direction. If shear forces occur in two directions within a section, separate checks will have to be carried out for each direction. This means that a beam can only have the following sets of loads of My, Mz, Fx, Fz, Mx (Fy - negligible small values) or My, Mz, Fx, Fz, Mx (Fy - negligible small values).

headings: Tabulating RC Frame Design results for AASHTO LRFD 8th and 9th Edition
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Frame Design Check RC Frame Design Check dialog. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC frame design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

When accessing detailed results from the Summary page the appropriate cross-section diagram showing the extent of the cracked zone and compression zone in the section will need to be selected from the droplist provided. In the Detailed Results panel, a statement will be made according to whether a section is cracked or uncracked, indicating whether a 'Cracked' or Uncracked' diagram showing the extent of the tension or compression in the section may be selected from the droplist.

headings: Tabulating RC Frame Design results for ACI 813-19
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Frame Design Check RC Frame Design Check dialog. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC frame design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.search_text: Summary results Tabulating RC Frame Design results for ACI 813-19 Application Manual (Bridge, Civil and Structural) RC Frame Design RC Frame Tabulated Results and Calculations Tabulating RC Frame Design results for ACI 813-19 Summary results Design RC Frame Design idh rcframe aci 318 19 detailed results.htm Summary results The summary page table shows the location of the check (the line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section), and the utilisation of the sections at the stated location for each design check. For each location the maximum utilisation calculated from the loadcases included in the RC Frame Design loadcase is provided. The Section name in the table is formed from the names of the Geometric line attribute and the referenced line reinforcement attribute. When tabulating details for tapered members the Section name will also include a parametric distance value to indicate where along the length of line the section applies. When viewing detailed results for a Summary check, an interaction surface diagram can also be obtained. See Obtaining detailed results for a selected row Obtaining detailed results for a selected row .

topics.text: Detailed results panel The content of the detailed results panel depends upon the tab displayed when the row on that page was selected. When accessing detailed results from the Summary page the appropriate cross-section diagram showing the extent of the cracked zone and compression zone in the section will need to be selected from the droplist provided. When one of the design check tabs such as strength check, or 'Control of cracking check' is selected the results related to the RC section and only the results related to the design check are listed, and only the cross-section chart for that selection can be drawn. In the Detailed Results panel, a statement will be made according to whether a section is cracked or uncracked, indicating whether a 'Cracked' or Uncracked' diagram showing the extent of the tension or compression in the section may be selected from the droplist.

topics.text: Cross-section charts The following cross-section charts can be drawn: Strength limit check (22.3 and 22.4 - Section at nominal resistance Distribution of flexural reinforcement (24.3) - 'Cracked' section Shear z and torsion (22.5 and 22.7) - 'Uncracked' section Shear y and torsion (22.5 and 22.7) - 'Uncracked' section Each diagram for the strength check contains information about the neutral axis, the compression part of the concrete (stresses=0) and the compression part of the concrete (constant stress-strain relation for concrete). topics.title: Table content explained
toc_path: RC Frame Tabulated Results and Calculations
Tabulating RC Frame Design results for AS5100.5-2017
headings: Tabulating RC Frame Design results for AS5100.5-2017
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Frame Design Check RC Frame Design Check dialog. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC frame design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.text: Detailed results The content of the detailed results depends upon the tab displayed when the row on that page was selected. When accessing detailed results from the Summary page the appropriate cross-section diagram showing the extent of the cracked zone and compression zone in the section will need to be selected from the droplist provided. When one of the design check tabs such as Strength Check, or Crack Control Check is selected the results related to the RC section and only the results related to the design check are listed, and only the cross-section chart for that selection can be drawn. In the Detailed Results panel, in the Crack Control check section, a statement will be made according to whether a section is cracked or uncracked, indicating whether a 'Cracked' or Uncracked' diagram showing the extent of the tension or compression in the section may be selected from the droplist.

The region of Europe is included in the list, offering calculations to EN1992 with defaults based on Recommended values from the main Eurocode documents. This option, with or without modification of values, may be of particular use for countries where a National Annex is not yet supported, or the National Annex simply adopts the Recommended Values. For some codes global settings applicable to the design checks can be additionally defined. toc_path: RC Frame Tabulated Results and Calculations
Tabulating RC Frame Design results for CSA S6-14 and CSA S6:19
headings: Tabulating RC Frame Design results for CSA S6-14 and CSA S6:19
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Frame Design Check RC Frame Design Check dialog. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC frame design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.text: Detailed results The content of the detailed results depends upon the tab displayed when the row on that page was selected. When accessing detailed results from the Summary page the appropriate cross-section diagram showing the extent of the cracked zone and compression zone in the section will need to be selected from the droplist provided. When one of the design check tabs such as ULS check, or Control of cracking check is selected the results related to the RC section and only the results related to the design check are listed, and only the cross-section chart for that selection can be drawn. In the Detailed Results panel, a statement will be made according to whether a section is cracked or uncracked, indicating whether a 'Cracked' or Uncracked' diagram showing the extent of the tension or compression in the section may be selected from the droplist.

headings: Tabulating RC Frame Design results for EN1992-1-1 and EN1992-2
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Frame Design Check RC Frame Design Check dialog. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC frame design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.text: Detailed results The content of the detailed results depends upon the tab displayed when the row on that page was selected. When accessing detailed results from the Summary page the appropriate cross-section diagram showing the extent of the cracked zone and compression zone in the section will need to be selected from the droplist provided. When one of the design check tabs such as ULS Check, or SLS (Crack Control) Check is selected the results related to the RC section and only the results related to the design check are listed, and only the cross-section chart for that selection can be drawn. In the Detailed Results panel, in the SLS Stress Limitation check section, a statement will be made according to whether a section is cracked or uncracked, indicating whether a 'Cracked' or Uncracked' diagram showing the extent of the tension or compression in the section may be selected from the droplist.

toc_path: RC Frame Tabulated Results and Calculations
Tabulating RC Frame Design results for IRC:112-2011
headings: Tabulating RC Frame Design results for IRC:112-2011
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Frame Design Check RC Frame Design Check dialog. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC frame design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.title: Overview
topics.text: Overview Design code checking of reinforced concrete beams/columns (decks/piers) can be carried out for a specified design code. This includes Strength/ULS and SLS checks based on bi-axial bending with overall tension/compression, shears, torsion, stress limits, minimum and maximum areas of reinforcement and crack widths or spacing considerations as appropriate. The checks are performed as a results processing operation following the solving of a model and requires the inclusion of reinforcement arrangements within the geometric line attribute as well as the assignment of design code specific RC frame design attributes to lines in the model that represent concrete members. RC frame design is available for use with selected Bridge and Civil software products only, and only for licences that support this facility.

topics.title: Meshing and analysis considerations
topics.text: Meshing and analysis considerations Lines representing reinforced concrete frame members must be assigned a 3-dimensional beam line mesh (thick beam, thick cross section beam, thick beam with torsional warping, thick cross section beam with torsional warping, thin beam, semiloof beam, semiloof cross section beam). Section capacity checks for selected members can be carried out at nodes, internal points or at inspection locations. Because of this any number of elements could be assigned to a line but using an excessive element assignment will increase the time required to carry out the design checks. It is recommended that lines should be assigned at least 2 elements and preferably a minimum of 4 elements.

Define/edit geometric line attributes Define/edit geometric line attributes , to include line reinforcement line reinforcement , which in turn references one or more section reinforcement section reinforcement utilities. The geometric line attributes must be assigned to the lines in the model which represent concrete members. Specify the design code Specify the design code to be used for the check by selecting the Design> RC Frame Design menu item. Define reinforced concrete material Define reinforced concrete material and assign to all lines representing reinforced concrete members. Define RC frame design attributes Define RC frame design attributes . These provide design related information and should be assigned to all lines representing reinforced concrete members. topics.title: Notes
toc_path: Carrying out a reinforced concrete frame design check
headings: Carrying out a reinforced concrete frame design check
topics.text: Notes The use of reinforced concrete materials and reinforcement arrangements is for design check calculations only. The analysis is unaffected and carried out using the gross concrete section. Because section and line reinforcement details and RC frame design attributes have no impact on a structural analysis they can be defined and assigned either before or after a model has been initially solved. When carrying out RC frame design checks the units used to create a model are automatically converted into units required by the design code chosen for the design check. The modelling units of the model itself are not changed. This would allow for a model to be constructed in US imperial units, and a design check on that model to be made to a metric design code, or vice-versa.

topics.title: RC frame design attributes
topics.text: RC frame design attributes Reinforced Concrete frame design attributes are used to specify additional information about the design checks (information that is specific to the Code of Practice and to the member in question). Attributes are defined using the Attributes> Design> RC Frame Design... menu item, which is available in Bridge and Civil software products only, and for licences that support this facility. Prior to defining an attribute a supported RC Frame design code RC Frame design code must have been chosen. Typical information defined in a RC frame design attribute includes: Beam and column minimum reinforcement ratios Calculation methodologies for the various checks Code of Practice specific parameters for both Strength/ULS (flexural, shear, torsion) and SLS (stress limitation and crack control) check Creep parameters Orientation of the neutral axis Once defined, a Design attribute entry is created in the Attributes Treeview ready for assignment to selected lines representing concrete members in a model.

topics.title: Specify the RC frame design results required
toc_path: Specify the RC frame design results required
headings: Specify the RC frame design results required
topics.text: Specify the RC frame design results required Use the Design> RC Frame Design Results menu item to bring together loadcases / combinations appropriate to specific design checks and identify members for which calculations are required, along with other calculation options. One or more RC Frame Results objects must be created in order to view graphical or tabular results from design check calculations. The settings available on the dialog are described here. On completion an RC Frame Design loadcase / results container entry is created in the Analyses Treeview. Multiple RC Frame Design results loadcases can be defined enabling design calculations to be carried out for different extents (lines) within a model, at different locations along each line (internal points, nodes only or inspection locations only), and for chosen load groups and design checks. For example, with large models, setting up an RC Frame Design results entry for all beams in a model and a separate one for all columns will limit the number of design checks to be carried out each time a change is made to one or the other.

topics.text: Design check locations Design checks applicable to a chosen design code can be individually selected for the following locations: Averaged nodal - results for nodes at the ends and within each beam element that is assigned to a member are averaged at each node. Unaveraged nodal - results for nodes at the ends and within each beam element that is assigned to a member are unaveraged at each node. Internal points - the internal (calculation) points for each element. Each element is discretised into ten divisions for calculation and results viewing purposes. This produces nine equally-spaced points along each element with two end points coinciding with the nodal locations of the element. Inspection locations - a defined position of interest on a line for results extraction / viewing purposes. When choosing this option at least one inspection location inspection location must be assigned to each line in the model that represents a reinforced concrete member. Note that inspection locations used in isolation may not pick-up extreme values. Viewing of RC frame design results for nodes will enable an initial design check to be carried out. The time taken to carry out a design check is directly related to the number of nodes, internal points or inspection locations used.

topics.text: Notes: For a design check location of 'Node', a colour-filled spot contour plot is produced showing the value of the chosen component at each node. For a design check location of 'Internal Point', the values obtained at each internal point are interpolated to create line contours. These can also be drawn on fleshed sections. When making changes to geometric attributes a model must be re-solved to see the result of that change. When making changes to reinforcement quantities there is no need to re-solve the model; the RC Frame Design calculations will be automatically re-run according to the changes made. RC frame design checks cannot be carried out if geometric properties used in different analyses that are set-up within a single model are in conflict.

topics.text: Tabulating RC frame design check results Utilisation results and more detailed information can be obtained by right-clicking on the RC Frame Design loadcase / results container in the Analyses Treeview and selecting the Show Results menu item. A results table is created showing a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Frame Design Check dialog. For any page, when a row in the table is selected, more detailed results showing calculations made can be obtained by double-clicking on the row, or by pressing the Detailed Results for Selected Row button. These tables of results and detailed results can be added to a model report. Results can also be filtered using options available. For a ULS check a resistance interaction surface may also be created by pressing the Resistance Interaction Surface (All the internal forces included) button. Tabulated results output differs for each supported design code. Refer to the appropriate design code for details. topics.title: RC Frame Resistance Interaction Surface Diagrams
toc_path: RC Frame Resistance Interaction Surface Diagrams
headings: RC Frame Resistance Interaction Surface Diagrams
topics.text: RC Frame Resistance Interaction Surface Diagrams RC frame design RC frame design results can be viewed as a resistance interaction surface diagram. The diagram can be plotted and viewed in 2D or 3D from coordinates that correspond to the values of the internal forces (My, Mz, Fx) for a selected section. A diagram key shows contours of axial force, with red lines indicating an axial compression capacity of the section, and blue lines indicating the tension capacity of the section. All points inside the interaction surface meet the ULS resistance requirements. All points outside an interaction surface do not meet the ULS resistance (or Strength Limit State) requirements. When tabulating RC frame design results interaction surface diagrams can be created: For a single location - for a location defined by a line, element, internal point and section type within a model, considering just the internal forces for that location. For all locations - for all locations of a section type considering all the internal forces for all locations of that section.

topics.title: Bending only (Wood-Armer)
toc_path: Background to RC Slab/Wall Design Calculations
headings: Background to RC Slab/Wall Design Calculations
topics.text: Bending only (Wood-Armer) Where a reinforced concrete slab is subject to a general set of bending and twisting moments (Mx, My, Mxy), these must be rationalised into components which can be used to design the 4 layers of reinforcement – top and bottom, X and Y directions. The method used here is that attributed to Wood & Armer (1969), which optimises the reinforcement requirements based on total weight of reinforcement. Codes of Practice generally set out principles or rules in terms of the flexural resistance of beams. In accordance with industry practice, the RC Slab/Wall Design software option uses these rules together with Wood-Armer moments to determine ULS reinforcement requirements. To prevent excessive compression in the concrete, due to the combined effect of moments in orthogonal directions, Cope & Clark (1984) recommend that slabs are “tension controlled” (sometimes termed “under-reinforced”), i.e. the resistance of the section should be controlled by yielding of the tensile reinforcement rather than crushing of the concrete. Adding compression steel is advised against, and accordingly the RC Slab/Wall Design option assumes that all reinforcement specified is tensile. RC Slab/Wall Design in LUSAS enables users to check that the slab is tension-controlled, by use of the appropriate contour option. The plot is based on a ratio, the specifics of which are detailed according to the Code of Practice, calculated at each node. If the slab is not "tension-controlled", reinforcement calculations may be unconservatively inaccurate.

If the slab is not "tension-controlled", reinforcement calculations may be unconservatively inaccurate.

topics.title: Bending and in-plane forces (Sandwich model)
toc_path: Background to RC Slab/Wall Design Calculations
headings: Background to RC Slab/Wall Design Calculations
topics.text: Bending and in-plane forces (Sandwich model) The sandwich model implemented in LUSAS is based upon the sandwich model described in Annex LL of EN 1992-2:2005 Eurocode 2: Design of concrete structures – Part2: Concrete bridges – Design and detailing rules. Annex LL accounts for the effects of transverse and in-plane shears and removes the "fixed sandwich layer depth" limitation of Clark-Nielsen. It divides a shell element into three layers. The outer or cover layers are considered to act as membranes resisting the direct in-plane forces along with the resolved forces from the bending and twisting moments. The central core resists transverse shearing forces only. Whilst the cited code only requires the sandwich model to be used when elements are considered to have cracked, in LUSAS it is used conservatively for all cases. The use of the Sandwich model overcomes limitations in the use of equations presented by Wood and Armer and others for the design or assessment of reinforced concrete slabs, which can be unsafe in some cases as they fail to take account of important features of the behaviour of concrete shells in bi-axial bending such as: Reduced effectiveness with skewed, heavy reinforcement. More specifically: Neutral axis depth is influenced by forces in all sets of reinforcement Bending in certain directions could result in “over-reinforced” failure mechanisms without yielding of the reinforcement. Reduced effectiveness in anticlastic bending. More specifically: The resistance of the concrete shell is sensitive to the magnitude and form of the applied bending moment field The concrete strength in compression is reduced due to transverse tension (tension softening) Tension softening may be influenced by a rotation of the compressive stress direction between elastic behaviour and ultimate resistance.

topics.title: Bending only (Principal moments)
toc_path: Background to RC Slab/Wall Design Calculations
headings: Background to RC Slab/Wall Design Calculations
topics.text: Bending only (Principal moments) Where a reinforced concrete slab is subject to a general set of bending and twisting moments, it may be reasonably assumed that tensile cracks will form perpendicular to the directions of principal moments. Codes of Practice generally set out principles or rules in terms of cracking in beams, where, by nature, the principal moments are aligned with the direction of the reinforcement. Such methods can, however, be applied to slabs (where the principal moments may not coincide with the reinforcement directions), with the crack assumed perpendicular to the principal moment direction, using an equivalent area of reinforcement. The equivalent area of reinforcement used by the RC Slab Design option is that given by the expression attributed to Cope & Clark (1984): Where: A n = equivalent area of steel per unit width in the n-direction A i = area of steel per unit width in the i-direction (of total N layers of steel) at the face considered. α i = angle between the direction of ith layer of reinforcement and the direction perpendicular to the crack The equivalent area calculated using this expression is described by Cope & Clark as being conservative for synclastic bending but unconservative for anticlastic bending. However the alternative equation offered by the same authors gives singularities where α = ±45°, and furthermore the equation above appears to give conservative answers compared to the method of Jofriet & McNeice. It is therefore adopted for all crack width calculations in the RC Slab/Wall Design option within LUSAS. The crack widths calculated are therefore notionally measured in the direction of the principal moment, based on an effective area of reinforcing steel which includes contributions from the two reinforcement directions in the tension zone of the slab as appropriate. That said, the reinforcement most nearly orthogonal to the crack (or widest crack, if cracking occurs in two directions) must be identified as the “controlling” direction. The results are subscripted with x or y to identify which bars are notionally controlling the cracking. Contours allow identifying which bars to modify in order to most efficiently control cracking in the slab. Code of Practice rules for crack widths in beams generally include a reduction in consideration of the stiffening effect of tension carried by concrete that remains bonded to the reinforcement in the tensile zone at small strains. However, where reinforcement does not lie perpendicular to cracks, as has been described to be the case in slabs, whether the “tension stiffening” reduction should be included is a matter of debate. Cope & Clarke suggest that tension stiffening should be ignored completely when principal moments act at α>25° to the reinforcement. RC Slab/Wall Design in LUSAS offers crack check calculations with the tension stiffening component included, ignored (conservative) or interpolated. The “interpolated” option scales linearly from 0% tension stiffening at α=25°, to 100% at α=0°, and this is the default option. In the case of crack-width calculations, it may be necessary to nominate a long-term loadcase on the RC Slab/Wall Design : Crack Width Calculation Settings page, in which case the active loadcase is used for additional short-term loading.

topics.title: Bending and in-plane forces (principal stresses)
toc_path: Background to RC Slab/Wall Design Calculations
headings: Background to RC Slab/Wall Design Calculations
topics.text: Bending and in-plane forces (principal stresses) Crack widths are determined from steel strains computed in an effective steel area in the direction of the principal stress. Since bar spacings are required in the crack widths calculations these results are collated according to the x and y` directions which represent the reinforcement directions. The orientation of the principal stress determines which bar is “controlling” but both directions contribute to the effective steel area. The effective steel area is determined in the direction of the cracking plane. The neutral axis is calculated taking into account the presence of both applied force and moment, in the direction of the principal stress. The steel stress is therefore calculated by computing the forces in the steel and concrete resulting from the in-plane and bending effects as follows. From force equilibrium: Force in the steel Stress in the steel Force in the concrete Stress in the concrete Where F = In-plane force in the principal stress direction. Fc = Internal force in the concrete Fs = Internal force in the steel M = Moment in the principal stress direction. h = Height of the section x = Neutral axis accounting for in-plane and bending d = Effective depth of tensile steel reinforcement Notes The sign of the bending moment is changed to reflect the slab face being considered, the equations shown assume cracking at the bottom face where a negative moment causes tensile (positive) stress in the bottom face. Where the neutral axis is found to be outside the section and the section is therefore considered to be wholly in tension, the tensile force is distributed to the top and bottom bars, i.e. based on statics with the force assumed to act at the centre of the slab (h/2). The moment is then divided by the lever arm between the reinforcement layers.

topics.title: Reinforcement Design calculations.
topics.text: Reinforcement Design calculations. ULS reinforcement design or SLS crack checking may be selected, although for some Codes of Practice the latter is not available. ULS section design This option provides checks on flexural resistance based on assigned reinforcement arrangements. Bending only (Wood-Armer) Calculations are based on Wood-Armer moments and resistances determined ignoring reinforcement in the compression zone. Each of the four layers of reinforcement may be checked in turn. Bending and in-plane forces (Clark-Nielsen) Calculations are based upon Clark-Nielsen forces, which are calculated based on lever arms determined from the reinforcement arrangement specified in a RC slab reinforcement design attribute RC slab reinforcement design attribute when assigned to the model. SLS crack checking This option provides calculation of design crack widths for proposed reinforcement arrangements. Bending only (Principal moments) Calculations are based on principal moments and make allowance for the non-alignment of principal moments and reinforcement. Crack widths can be viewed according to the reinforcement direction "controlling" the crack, such that each of the four layers of reinforcement can be checked in turn. Bending and in-plane effects (Principal stresses) Calculations use principal stress to determine the orientation of the crack direction. The effective steel area is determined in the direction of the cracking plane. The neutral axis is calculated taking into account the presence of both applied force and moment. If crack width calculation is supported by the chosen design code additional parameters need to be specified on the Crack Width Calculation Settings dialog.

Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for AASHTO LRFD 5th to 9th Edition
headings: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for AASHTO LRFD 5th to 9th Edition
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Slab/Wall Design RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase/results dialog. Detailed results for any selected row are also available. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Clicking in a column header will sort the data in that column according to its content. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC slab/wall design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.text: Summary results The summary page table shows the location of the check (the section number, surface number, element and node (or inspection location), and the utilisations of the section at the stated location for each design check. For each location the maximum utilisation calculated from the loadcases included in the RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase is provided. The following results are provided: Util(Strength) - Maximum utilisation for 'Strength check'. For Slab/Wall Design Results Loadsets this only appears if the ULS check is ticked. Util(Asmin,Asmax) - Maximum utilisation from the 'Min-max reinforcement' check. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation. Util(Max) - Maximum utilisation from all checks carried out.

topics.text: Strength check (5.6) The 'Strength limit check' is carried out in accordance with clause 5.6. The table contains information describing the location of the check, the loadcase and, if relevant, the primary component for which the utilisation is applicable, the face/direction of the check, and provides the following value and results: Util(As) - Utilisation of reinforcement. Util(TC) - Utilisation of tension control. Not available for Clark-Nielsen. Util(Sc) - Utilisation of concrete stress. Not available for Wood-Armer. Util(Vc) - Utilisation of shear resistance without shear reinforcement. Util(Vmax) - Utilisation of the shear compression strut. Assh [in 2 /ft 2 ] - Area of steel provided per unit area in the face and direction considered. Util(Max) - Maximum utilisation for this check.

topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Slab/Wall Design RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase/results dialog. Detailed results for any selected row are also available. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Clicking in a column header will sort the data in that column according to its content. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC slab/wall design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

The table contains information describing the location of the check, the loadcase and, if relevant, the primary component for which the utilisation is applicable, the face/direction of the check, and provides the following value and results depending upon the settings made on the RC slab/wall design attribute for this code: Util(As) - Utilisation of reinforcement. topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Slab/Wall Design RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase/results dialog. Detailed results for any selected row are also available. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Clicking in a column header will sort the data in that column according to its content. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC slab/wall design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.text: Summary results The summary page table shows the location of the check (the section number, surface number, element and node (or inspection location), and the utilisations of the section at the stated location for each design check. For each location the maximum utilisation calculated from the loadcases included in the RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase is provided. The following results are provided: Util(Strength) - Maximum utilisation from the 'Strength' check. This only appears if the Strength check on the RC Slab/Wall Design Results dialog is ticked. Util(Asmin) - Maximum utilisation of the 'Min reinforcement' check. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation. Util(Max) - Maximum utilisation from all checks carried out.

topics.text: Enveloped results The enveloped results table contains information describing the location of the checks, the types of check, and provides the following results: Util(As) - Maximum utilisation of reinforcement out of all checks. This excludes the utilisation of the maximum reinforcement requirement, since the action that the user has to take differs if the reinforcement is more than required or less than required. Util(Max(As)) - Maximum utilisation of the maximum reinforcement check (if check exists). Util(TC) - Maximum utilisation of tension control. Not available for Clark-Nielsen. Util(Shear) - Maximum utilisation of the shear resistance from the concrete. Util(Sc) - Maximum utilisation of concrete stress among all checks. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation (if SLS crack control check is selected). Util(Max) - Maximum overall utilisation for each location.

Clause 9.4.1(b) for AS3600:2009. Clause 8.6.1(b) for walls designed as columns. Util(Asmin1) - Utilisation of the reinforcement area for the following check: Clause 9.5.1(a) for slabs or walls designed as slabs for AS3600:2018. Clause 9.4.1(b) for AS3600:2009. Clause 8.6.1(a) for walls designed as columns. Util(Asmin2) - Utilisation of reinforcement area for the following check: Clause 9.5.3 for slabs for AS3600:2018. Clause 9.4.1(b) for AS3600:2009. Clause 11.7.2 for walls. Util(CW) (for AS3600:2018 only) Utilisation of crack width (clause 9.5.2.2 for slabs or walls designed as slabs or clause 8.6.2.3 for walls designed as column). fs (for AS3600:2009 only) Steel stress. headings: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for AS5100.5-2017 and AS5100.5-2004
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Slab/Wall Design RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase/results dialog. Detailed results for any selected row are also available. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Clicking in a column header will sort the data in that column according to its content. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC slab/wall design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.text: Summary results The summary page table shows the location of the check (the section number, surface number, element and node (or inspection location), and the utilisations of the section at the stated location for each design check. Util(Asmin) - Maximum utilisation from the 'Min reinforcement' check. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation. Util(Max) - Maximum utilisation from all checks carried out.

topics.title: Table content explained
toc_path: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for BS 5400-4:1990
headings: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for BS 5400-4:1990
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Slab/Wall Design RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase/results dialog. Detailed results for any selected row are also available. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Clicking in a column header will sort the data in that column according to its content. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC slab/wall design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.title: Summary results
toc_path: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for BS 5400-4:1990
headings: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for BS 5400-4:1990
topics.text: Summary results The summary page table shows the location of the check (the section number, surface number, element and node (or inspection location), and the utilisations of the section at the stated location for each design check. For each location the maximum utilisation calculated from the loadcases included in the RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase is provided. The following results are provided: Util(ULS) - Maximum utilisation for the 'ULS' check. This only appears if the ULS check on the RC Slab/Wall design results dialog is ticked. Util(Asmin,Asmax) - Maximum utilisation for the 'Min-max reinforcement' check. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation. Util(SLS.S) - Maximum utilisation for SLS stress limitation. Util(Max) - Maximum utilisation from all checks carried out.

topics.title: Enveloped results
toc_path: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for BS 5400-4:1990
headings: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for BS 5400-4:1990
topics.text: Enveloped results The enveloped results table contains information describing the location of the checks, the types of check, and provides the following results: Util(As) - Maximum utilisation of reinforcement out of all checks. This excludes the utilisation of the maximum reinforcement requirement, since the action that the user has to take differs if the reinforcement is more than required or less than required. Util(Max(As)) - Maximum utilisation of the maximum reinforcement check (if check exists). Util(TC) - Maximum utilisation of tension control. Not available for Clark-Nielsen. Util(Sc) - Maximum utilisation of concrete stress among all checks. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation (if SLS crack control check selected). Util(Max) - Maximum overall utilisation for each location.

topics.text: Summary results The summary page table shows the location of the check (the section number, surface number, element and node (or inspection location), and the utilisations of the section at the stated location for each design check. For each location the maximum utilisation calculated from the loadcases included in the RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase is provided. The following results are provided: Util(ULS) - Maximum utilisation for the 'ULS' check. This only appears if the ULS check on the RC Slab/Wall design results dialog is ticked. Util(Asmin,Asmax) - Maximum utilisation for the 'Min-max reinforcement' check. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation. Util(Max) - Maximum utilisation from all checks carried out.

topics.text: Enveloped results The enveloped results table contains information describing the location of the checks, the types of check, and provides the following results: Util(As) - Maximum utilisation of reinforcement out of all checks. This excludes the utilisation of the maximum reinforcement requirement, since the action that the user has to take differs if the reinforcement is more than required or less than required. Util(Max(As)) - Maximum utilisation of the maximum reinforcement check (if check exists). Util(TC) - Maximum utilisation of tension control. Not available for Clark-Nielsen. Util(Sc) - Maximum utilisation of concrete stress among all checks. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation (if SLS crack control check selected). Util(Max) - Maximum overall utilisation for each location.

topics.title: Table content explained
toc_path: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for BS 8100-1:1997 & BS 8110-2:1985
headings: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for BS 8100-1:1997 & BS 8110-2:1985
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Slab/Wall Design RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase/results dialog. Detailed results for any selected row are also available. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Clicking in a column header will sort the data in that column according to its content. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC slab/wall design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

headings: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for CSA-S6:19, CSA-S6-14 and CSA S6-06
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Slab/Wall Design RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase/results dialog. Detailed results for any selected row are also available. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Clicking in a column header will sort the data in that column according to its content. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC slab/wall design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.text: Summary results The summary page table shows the location of the check (the section number, surface number, element and node (or inspection location), and the utilisations of the section at the stated location for each design check. For each location the maximum utilisation calculated from the loadcases included in the RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase is provided. The following results are provided: Util(ULS) - Maximum utilisation for the ULS check. This only appears if the ULS check on the RC Slab/Wall design results dialog is ticked. Util(Asmin,Asmax) - Maximum utilisation for the 'Min-max reinforcement' check. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation. Util(Max) - Maximum utilisation from all checks carried out.

topics.text: Enveloped results The enveloped results table contains information describing the location of the checks, the types of check, and provides the following results: Util(As) - Maximum utilisation of reinforcement out of all checks. This excludes the utilisation of the maximum reinforcement requirement since the action that the user has to take differs if the reinforcement is more than required or less than required. Util(Max(As)) - Maximum utilisation of the maximum reinforcement check (if check exists). Util(TC) - Maximum utilisation of tension control. Not available for Clark-Nielsen. Util(Shear) - Maximum utilisation of the shear resistance from the concrete. Util(Sc) - Maximum utilisation of concrete stress among all checks. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation (if SLS crack control check selected). Util(Max) - Maximum overall utilisation for each location.

All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Clicking in a column header will sort the data in that column according to its content. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC slab/wall design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.text: Summary results The summary page table shows the location of the check (the section number, surface number, element and node (or inspection location), and the utilisations of the section at the stated location for each design check. For each location the maximum utilisation calculated from the loadcases included in the RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase is provided. The following results are provided: Util(ULS) - Maximum utilisation for the 'ULS (6.1 & 6.2)' check. This only appears if the ULS check on the RC Slab/Wall design results dialog is ticked. Util(Asmin,Asmax) - Maximum utilisation for the 'Min-max reinforcement' check. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation. Util(SLS,S) - Maximum utilisation for SLS stress limitation. Util(AsCC) - Maximum utilisation of the minimum area of reinforcement for crack control check. Util(Max) - Maximum utilisation from all checks carried out.

topics.text: Enveloped results The enveloped results table contains information describing the location of the checks, the types of check, and provides the following results: Util(As) - Maximum utilisation of reinforcement out of all checks. This excludes the utilisation of the maximum reinforcement requirement, since the action that the user has to take differs if the reinforcement is more than required or less than required. Util(Max(As)) - Maximum utilisation of the maximum reinforcement check (if check exists). Util(TC) - Maximum utilisation of tension control. Not available for Clark-Nielsen. Util(Shear) - Maximum utilisation of the shear resistance from the concrete. Util(Sc) - Maximum utilisation of concrete stress among all checks. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation (if SLS crack control check selected). Util(Max) - Maximum overall utilisation for each location.

topics.text: Min-max reinforcement The table contains information describing the location of the check (surface, element, node, face/direction), member and rebar type (primary / secondary), and provides the following results: Util(Asmin1) - First check for minimum reinforcement utilisation. For slabs: Primary is calculated to clause 9.2.1.1 (1). Secondary is calculated to clause 9.3.1.1 (2). This is only relevant for one-way slabs. For two-way slabs, both directions of reinforcement will be treated as primary. For walls: Vertical and Horizontal is calculated to clause 11.7.1 Util(Asmin2) - Second check for minimum reinforcement utilisation. See column header pop-up for relevant slab and wall clauses and other details. For slabs: Primary is calculated to clause 9.2.1.1 (1). Secondary is calculated to clause 9.3.1.1 (2). For walls: Not applicable. Util(Asmax) - Utilisation of the maximium area of reinforcement. For slabs: Calculation is to clause 9.2.1.1 (3). For walls: Calculation is to clause 9.6.2 (1) Util(Max) - Maximum utilisation of all checks carried out.

topics.title: Table content explained
toc_path: RC Slab/Wall Tabulated Results and Calculations
Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for IRC:112-2011
headings: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for IRC:112-2011
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Slab/Wall Design RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase/results dialog. Detailed results for any selected row are also available. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Clicking in a column header will sort the data in that column according to its content. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC slab/wall design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for IRS:CBC-1997
headings: Tabulating RC Slab/Wall Design results for IRS:CBC-1997
topics.text: Table content explained The results table consists of a summary page and separate tabbed pages for each of the design checks requested in the RC Slab/Wall Design RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase/results dialog. Detailed results for any selected row are also available. All results tables contain information describing the location of each check (line, element/inspection location, node/internal point/index, section) and, when relevant, any internal forces used in the check (load, primary component, internal forces (Fx, My, Mz)). Utilisation values of greater than 1 are coloured red to identify over-utilised sections. A colour coded column at the right of the grid also provides an indication of utilisation capacities for each section location, with colours of grey, green, yellow, orange and red used when utilisations are under 0.7, from 0.7 to 0.8, 0.8 to 0.9, 0.9 to 1.0, and over 1.0 respectively. Clicking in a column header will sort the data in that column according to its content. Note that the column names and results listed are dependent upon the settings made in the RC slab/wall design attribute dialog for each code. Tooltips for each column header provide additional information, including references to applicable clauses.

topics.text: Summary results The summary page table shows the location of the check (the section number, surface number, element and node (or inspection location), and the utilisations of the section at the stated location for each design check. For each location the maximum utilisation calculated from the loadcases included in the RC Slab/Wall Design loadcase is provided. The following results are provided: Util(ULS) - The maximum utilisation from the ULS check. This only appears if the ULS check on the RC Slab/Wall design results dialog is ticked. Util(Asmin,Asmax) - Maximum utilisation of the Min-max reinforcement check. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation. Util(SLS.S) - Maximum utilisation for SLS stress limitation. Util(Max) - The maximum utilisation from all checks.

topics.text: Enveloped results The enveloped results table contains information describing the location of the checks, the types of check, and provides the following results: Util(As) - Maximum utilisation of reinforcement out of all checks. This excludes the utilisation of the maximum reinforcement requirement, since the action that the user has to take differs if the reinforcement is more than required or less than required. Util(Max(As)) - Maximum utilisation of the maximum reinforcement check (if check exists). Util(TC) - Maximum utilisation of tension control. Not available for Clark-Nielsen. Util(Sc) - Maximum utilisation of concrete stress among all checks. Util(CC) - Maximum crack control utilisation (if SLS crack control check selected). Util(Max) - Maximum overall utilisation for each location.
