topics.title: Adding New Network Licence Details
topics.text: Adding New Network Licence Details If you are installing a new network licence for the first time your network licence keys are supplied to you by LUSAS in a text file. Select the server to which you wish to add a new network licence. Select the button to browse to the location of the Licence Code text file supplied for your LUSAS software installation. The option to make this licence available to LUSAS on this (local) machine is enabled by default. If unchecked, the licence is only added to the server. Entering a licence name is optional. Notes A server name or IP Address of a known server can be manually entered if not discovered when the dialog was first initialised. If you are getting communication errors relating to a server and you suspect a clash of port numbers you may wish to communicate with a particular server on a different port. In this case, the port number can be entered in the server combo, separating the server name from the port with a colon. You must also alter the port on which the server in question is listening. This is done by running Administrative tools on the server machine and differs according to the operating system in use: If running Windows 2000/NT/Vista, on the server machine click Start menu> Settings > Control Panel, and double click Administrative Tools. If running Windows 7, on the server machine click Start menu> Control Panel, and double click Administrative Tools. If running Windows 8, on the server machine right-click on the main Start screen, click the magnifying glass and enter Administrative Tools into the search box If running Windows 8.1, on the server machine, on the main Start screen, click on the Apps down arrow and browse for Administrative Tools If running Windows 10, on the server machine click Start> All Apps and browse for Administrative Tools Once accessed: Double click Services , locate Sentinel RMS Development Kit License Manager and double click it. Click Stop Enter -PORT <your port number> in the start parameters text box. Click Start See also: For further information please see the following links to the LUSAS User Area of the LUSAS website: Security Key Support Security Key Support

topics.title: Memory Usage Information
topics.text: Memory Usage Information This page of the LUSAS configuration utility LUSAS configuration utility shows the physical memory (RAM) installed in your computer, and also how much of it is in use. It also shows the paged (disk) memory which is available for use as virtual memory and how much of it is in use. The amount of memory allocated by the currently selected version of LUSAS Solver is shown. You may change this latter amount by using the Modify Solver memory allocations button. See also: For further information please see the following links to the LUSAS User Area of the LUSAS website: How do I optimise LUSAS Solver memory allocation? topics.title: Modify Memory Usage
topics.text: Modify Memory Usage Pressing the Modify Solver memory allocations button on the Memory Usage of the LUSAS Configuration Utility LUSAS Configuration Utility page presents this page which lets you specify the amount of memory which LUSAS Solver should use and values of related system parameters. NLPZ determines the size of the LUSAS memory in which all the LUSAS calculations are performed NPGS specifies the maximum number of data records allowed in the LUSAS data cache MXELGP specifies the maximum number of elements in a group. From V15.0 onwards it is generally recommended that the memory allocation settings for Solver are not changed from their installation default settings. Owing to the wide range of hardware configurations available and the difference in magnitude between different LUSAS analyses, it is impossible to identify a single set of optimum values for all users. Advice should be sought from LUSAS technical support (support@lusas.com) if you intend to make changes to your PC's memory usage settings. topics.title: Temporary Files
topics.text: Temporary Files This page of the LUSAS Configuration Utilit LUSAS Configuration Utilit y shows the Windows virtual memory (page) file location(s), the Windows temporary files location, and the LUSAS Modeller and LUSAS Solver temporary file locations. By default, LUSAS Modeller and LUSAS Solver store temporary files in the same folder as Windows, but it is suggested you specify an alternative folder, e.g. C:\Temp Enter the folder names which LUSAS Modeller and LUSAS Solver should use to store temporary files, e.g. C:\Temp Use the browse buttons (...) to see a list of available drives, and to easily locate your chosen folder(s). Press the Clean up buttons to remove old temporary files from your hard disk. This will make more disk space available to LUSAS. Each button acts only on the folder to which it is adjacent. topics.title: Colour By Connectivity
topics.text: Colour By Connectivity Allows the geometry to be coloured according to the connectivity of its parent features. Features are drawn in a contracted state in different colours according to the number of higher order features that are connected to them. Colouring surfaces by Line Connectivity enables coincident lines or edges to be identified. Colouring volumes by Surface Connectivity enables coincident surfaces to be identified. Note. Connectivity issues may arise when importing geometry because coincident imported points and lines are not within the merge tolerance. See also: Using colour for geometry Using colour for geometry

topics.title: Line Mesh Assignments
topics.text: Line Mesh Assignments For 3D beam elements and joint elements the element xy - plane will have been defined on assignment. Beta angle This is the rotation angle between the line axes and the element axes. Used to orientate a beam's cross-section when a geometric line attribute is assigned to a line, and to orientate local loading. Ignore local coords assigned to point When joints are defined between non-coincident lines the local x-axis is orientated from Master (Line 1) to Slave (Line 2) and the element local z is then defined in the xZ plane unless the local x axis is aligned to the global Z axis in which case the element local z axis is aligned with the global Y axis. When joints between coincident lines are assigned a Line Mesh the local axes are aligned to the global axes. This method is also used when no Local Coordinate is assigned to the Master line By point in selection memory (Not applicable for line interface mesh assignment) By specified local coordinates The element axes are defined using a previously defined local coordinate.

topics.title: Orientation
topics.text: Orientation The composite orientation will be taken from one of the following: Local element axes Uses the element axes which are taken from the surface axes. Local coordinate Local coordinate If a local coordinate has been defined it may be used to align the material direction of the composite layup. Notes Composite properties should only be assigned to Surfaces and Volumes which are meshed with elements which accommodate composite properties. See Solver Reference Manual for details. Composite attributes are uniform over the assigned feature. Composites may also be orientated using draping. See also: Composites Composites

topics.title: Loading Assignments
topics.text: Loading Assignments Shows the unassigned and assigned loading attributes. A load attribute can be assigned to a geometry feature more than once, therefore assigned attributes still appear in the unassigned list. To assign a load attribute select the attribute in the Available box and click on the Add>> button. Then select the same attribute in the Assigned box and specify the Loadcase and Load factor. It is possible to assign load attributes to a feature more than once. To deassign a load attribute select the attribute in the Assigned box and click on the <<Remove button. Assigned in active loadcase , when selected, displays in the Assigned box only those loadings that have been assigned for the active loadcase. When de-selected will allow selection of loadcase in drop-down list to show assigned loadings for that loadcase. Details... shows the projection method and inclusion/exclusion setting for loads that extend outside a search area. Thsi is only applicable for discrete point, patch and compound loads and requires the assigned loadcase to be selected for the button to be selectable. Note. Only load attributes that are applicable to the currently selected geometry type are listed. See also: About Loading About Loading

topics.title: Attributes
topics.text: Attributes General Options Apply concentrated loads in cylindrical coordinates for Fourier elements (LUSAS Solver option 202). Body force given as acceleration This option is turned on by default. Turning it off converts body forces to global loads per unit volume. (LUSAS Solver option 48). Activate spring supports in undeformed location - Description required Allow modification of LUSAS generated attributes overrides the default behaviour of not allowing any changes to be made to Modeller-generated attributes such as loadings generated as a result of carrying out cable tuning analysis, vehicle load optimisation, prestress calculations, and rail track analysis. Slideline Options Suppress stringent slave search For simpler geometries, such as flat surfaces in contact, a slight reduction in processing time may be achieved by suppressing the "stringent" local node search but this is not usually recommended. (LUSAS Solver option 184). See the Theory Manual for more details. Suppress initial slide - surface stiffness check Scaling of the slideline stiffnesses is automatically invoked at the beginning of each analysis to account for bodies having significantly different material properties. This facility can be suppressed. (LUSAS Solver option 185 ). See the Theory Manual for more details. Suppress initial penetration check The coordinates of all contact nodes which are determined to have penetrated prior to the commencement of the analysis are reset normally to the contacted surface. This resetting of coordinates is not available for tied slidelines. This should be set if performing an interference fit type of analysis. (LUSAS Solver option 186). See the Theory Manual for more details. See also: Model Properties - Attributes Model Properties - Attributes

topics.title: General
topics.text: General Title Brief description of the current model as entered in the New Model startup dialog. Analysis category Defines the category of analysis that will be carried out with this model. Analysis category choices are 2D Grillage/Plate, 2D Inplane, 2D Axisymmetric, and 3D. An analysis category must be chosen when a model is first created. It can be changed on the Model Properties dialog, but this should be used with caution since subsequent dialog choices made may not be supported in certain levels of the software, or may be inappropriate for a particular type of analysis. Only show compatible options When checked, shows only those menu items, dialog options and settings that are relevant for the stated analysis category. When unchecked, will show dialog options and settings irrelevant of the analysis category set. This permits changing the analysis category on attribute dialogs that support this facility on a case-by-case basis and should be used with caution. Model units Specifies the modelling units. Output in feet and inches (only if imperial units are set) ensures that modelling units used to define coordinates and lengths are reported in feet and inches, instead of just feet or just inches. For example, a length may be output as 5'11.5", rather than 71.5" or 5.92'. Timescale units dictate how time-based values are displayed on dialogs during modelling, and how they are output when processing results. Units can be specified as seconds, minutes, hours, days or increments. Precision shown in dialogs Controls the number of significant figures or decimal places displayed in the dialogs. Decimal marker specifies how decimal points should be handled. Options are: Follow Windows, UK/US decimal point, and European comma formats. Vertical axis Set automatically by setting the Analysis category for new models. Used to determine the direction that gravity loading will be applied if added using the Bridge or Civil > Gravity menu item. It is also used to define the initial vertical axis and orientation of element types and library items as displayed on the Geometric Line dialog prior to them being added to a model. It also defines the model orientation viewed when using the isometric, dimetric and trimetric views. Note that changing the Analysis category (see above) only changes the vertical axis if it cannot remain the same because it would be invalid for the analysis category chosen. Gravity - Value set for the acceleration of free fall, as used when creating a Gravity loading from the Bridge of Civil menu item, and in a number of attribute definitions. See also: Model Properties Model Properties

topics.title: Geometry
topics.text: Geometry The method by which the geometry is displayed is controlled using the Geometry Geometry drawing layer. Merge Options Action controls the criteria that must be satisfied before features sharing a common definition will be merged. New geometry unmergable sets the merge status of all new features to Unmergable rather than the default which is Mergable. Tolerance controls the distance within which Point features must lie before they will be considered for merging. Note: The merge tolerance should only be changed with extreme caution because changing it from its default value can lead to instability of the underlying geometry engine. See Merging Features Merging Features for more details. Drawing defaults (faceting) The default faceting Lines and Surfaces buttons provide access to the number of facets used for shading. Increasing the number of facets improves the shaded geometry visualisation but takes longer to display. See Facet Density Facet Density for more details. Active Local Coordinate Sets the coordinate system as either the Global coordinate or any defined local Cartesian, cylindrical or spherical coordinate. If a local coordinate local coordinate is set activate then all subsequent geometry definition is carried out in transformed coordinates. Advanced button permits changing of the splitting, creation, hole removal and merge defaults See also Model Properties - Geometry Model Properties - Geometry

topics.title: Line faceting
topics.text: Line faceting By default, lines are assigned a facet density which is used in visualisation. Facet density effectively controls how smooth a line will look when drawn to the screen. Straight lines, arcs and splines are all drawn using facets of a line length that can be defined in a number of ways. The default facet density may be changed prior to geometry definition from the Geometry tab of the Model Properties Model Properties dialog or after geometry definition by selecting the appropriate Lines and Surfaces and modifying the facet density from the Geometry> Line> Facet density menu item. Facet density can be specified for the following features: Straight lines Arc lines All other types (splines for example) For lines, arcs or spline features the facet density may be specified by stating one of the following: Minimum number of facets - The number of straight lines used to represent the feature when drawn Maximum facet length The maximum length of line used to represent a facet. This is specified in model units. Maximum deviation (For arcs and splines only) The perpendicular offset distance from the mid-point of the facet line representing a segment of arc to the true drawn mid-point position of the segment of arc that it represents. Minimum adjacent angl e The internal angle between adjacent facets From the above it can be seen that either increasing the number of facets, or reducing the facet length, or reducing the maximum deviation, or increasing the minimum adjacent angle would all lead to a greater facet density. Note that facet density only affects the display of the geometric feature and not the actual geometric accuracy of the model. See also: Model Properties - Geometry Model Properties - Geometry

topics.title: Surface faceting
topics.text: Surface faceting By default, surfaces are assigned a facet density which is used in visualisation. Facet density effectively controls how smooth a surface will look when drawn to the screen. Surfaces are drawn using facets that are triangular. The default facet density may be changed prior to geometry definition from the Geometry tab of the Model Properties Model Properties dialog or after geometry definition by selecting the appropriate Lines and Surfaces and modifying the facet density from the Geometry> Surface> Facet density menu item. The facet density may be specified by stating one of the following: Maximum facet length The maximum length of one side of a facet triangle and is specified in model units. Maximum deviation The perpendicular offset distance from the mid-point of the facet triangle representing a segment of surface to the true drawn mid-point position of the segment of surface that it represents. Minimum number - The number of faceting triangles to be used to represent the surface when drawn. This can be set individually for Planar surfaces, Surfaces with a seam (such as cylinders) and Other surfaces - such as complex boolean surfaces. From the above it can be seen that either reducing the facet length, or reducing the maximum deviation, or increasing the minimum number of facets would all lead to a greater facet density. Notes Facet density only affects the display of the surface and not the actual geometric accuracy of the model. See also: Model Properties - Geometry Model Properties - Geometry

topics.title: Mesh settings
topics.text: Mesh settings Wireframe Displays the element mesh as a wireframe using the pen specified. Only the visible mesh lines are drawn. Transparent Displays a solid filled mesh with a transparency. Solid Displays the mesh as solid panels using the colour specified. Click on the coloured square to change the colour used. Maximum shade (for solid mesh only) A percentage value that controls how dark a solid mesh colour becomes (with respect to black) when the feature or object on which they are displayed is rotated into the plane of the screen. The default value of 60% darkens a colour by 60% of the difference between the defined colour and black and ensures that meshes drawn on orthogonal surfaces are shaded sufficiently to distinguish the separate sides of the features. Lower values of shade will lessen the difference, higher values increase the difference. Hidden edges Displays element edges and not just those of the the visible element faces. Internal edges Displays internal element edges. Show nodes Draws the mesh nodes. Nodes define the vertices of elements. Outline only Displays only the outline of the mesh for each assigned feature. This is also useful for spotting cracks or discontinuities in the mesh due to features not being merged or equivalenced correctly. The Threshold (deg) value controls when edges of elements are drawn. Edges of adjacent elements are drawn when the angle between the normals of adjacent elements exceeds the threshold value. Show normals Displays the element normal for Surface elements Joints offset distance Show element axes Displays the element axes as a local axis set. Orientations only if selected Displays the surface normal or element axes only if the element is selected. % of elements remaining Shrinks the elements to the percentage specified. Colour by Enables the mesh colour to be changed. Mesh colour - colours elements in default mesh colour. Group - colours elements by group. Connectivity - colours element edges by number of neighbours. Element Type - colours elements by element type. Normals - colours elements by surface normal direction. Note. The arrow sizes used for element axes and normals are defined on the Default tab of the Model Properties Model Properties . topics.text: Meshing Equivalence Defines the default nodal equivalence tolerance used in a equivalence attribute. Tolerance A default value of 1e-3 is set. Automatic (if selected) carries out equivalencing automatically for all nodes in the model and no equivalence attribute assignment is required. See Nodal Equivalencing Nodal Equivalencing for details. Line Mesh Defaults Default line divisions Sets the default number of mesh divisions on a line and the maximum subtended angle per element for an arc or splines. Default angle subtended If an element exceeds the max subtended angle the number of divisions on the arc or spline will be increased. Default beam orientation method Orientate beams and columns using model vertical axis When selected, identifies the alignment of the beams present in a supported third-party import file, or for beams within the model, and sets the beam element axes for each beam to a suitable orientation to represent either a vertical column or a horizontal beam, as typically used in modelling building frames. Unselected, the beam element axes for each beam are set to the default LUSAS orientation. Miscellaneous Create a group of objects that failed to mesh after meshing creates a group named $failedToMeshObjects which contains all features which failed to mesh. topics.title: Advanced meshing parameters
topics.text: Advanced meshing parameters Draw failed parts of mesh only - draws those parts of the mesh that failed to mesh Linearise line / surface element edges Moves the position of the mid-side nodes on quadratic elements to lie on a straight line connecting the corner nodes. Constrain adjacent linear/quadratic edges forces mid-side nodes on lines or surfaces to be averaged between the corner/end node positions. This option is turned on by default. Element edge collapsing invokes edge collapsing edge collapsing which removes elements/faces with short edges and small subtended angles by merging them with neighbouring elements. Irregular tet meshing specifies the number of the passes and attempts to be made by the tetrahedral mesh generation when attempting to mesh a volume. Script to run after meshing allows running of a user-defined script after meshing as, for example, if a quality check was desired to be run on mesh quality. topics.title: Averaging Options
topics.text: Averaging Options Results averaging options are accessed via the Model Properties dialog or the Model Properties control object in the Analyses Treeview. Averaging options can only be specified to be common for all analyses. By default in LUSAS Modeller, averaging of results is done for all situations where it is appropriate. Where averaging is inappropriate, multiple values instead of an averaged value are displayed. The Averaging Options dialog allows averaging rules to be applied to state when results averaging should and should not take place between adjacent pairs of elements in line, surface and volume features. For each pair of elements that is considered, if all the averaging rules "pass", then averaging of results across that pair of elements is permitted. The following rules are considered:

topics.title: Averaging rules / logic
topics.text: Averaging rules / logic Any elements that are meshed in the same feature are assumed to be suitable for averaging. This is a fundamental rule and as such does not appear in the user interface. The presence of this implicit rule means that all the rules below can assume that the elements are from different features. Note that this fundamental rule is not considered when transforming results to element local directions. Feature rule: Are the elements from different features? If so, there is a discontinuity. If not, check the next rule. Note that switching this rule 'on' makes all other rules below irrelevant. Visibility rule: Do the elements have different visibilities? If so, there is a discontinuity. If not, check the next rule. Junction rule: Is there a junction at this location? If so, there is a discontinuity. If not, check the next rule. Common LOF assignment rule: Does the common lower order feature between the two features have any attribute assignments? If so, there is a discontinuity. If not, check the next rule. Different assignments rule: Do elements have different attribute assignments? If so, there is a discontinuity. If not, check the next rule. Angle exceeds rule: Do element axes differ by more than a user-defined angular tolerance (default 12 degrees)? If so, there is a discontinuity. If not, check the next rule. There is no discontinuity present, so averaging between the pair of elements under consideration is allowed. For more details on averaging rules see Results Averaging Results Averaging Note Direct Method Influence analysis chooses what to average based upon the settings in force at the time when the DMI attribute is assigned. Because of this, subsequently changing the averaging options has no effect on the results viewed from a DMI analysis. See also: Solution Options Solution Options

topics.title: Coupled Analysis Control Options
topics.text: Coupled Analysis Control Options Coupled analysis options can be accessed via the Coupled analysis options object in the Analyses Treeview. Coupled analysis options can only be specified to be common for all analyses. They allow control of a coupled analysis coupled analysis . Coupling type defines which analysis to run first, Thermal first, Structural first, or Hygro-thermal first. Parallel coupling requires both analyses to run simultaneously such that the temperatures from the thermal analysis are read into the structural analysis and the displacements from the structural analysis into the thermal analysis. If the temperatures are to be calculated in a thermal analysis and then transferred to a structural analysis this option is not required. Initialise reference temperatures takes the first temperature distribution from the thermal analysis and uses them as the reference temperatures in the structural analysis. Suppress recalculation of view factors in coupled analysis Turns on/off the view factor recalculation. The option should be turned on when the radiation surface radiation surface geometry is unchanged by the structural analysis to suppress the re-calculation of view factors. (LUSAS Solver option 256). Step coupling is used for coupling thermal to structural analysis such that the nonlinear increment is used to control the coupling steps. Time coupling is used for coupling thermal to structural/transient analysis such that the time is used to control the coupling steps. First data read and first data write are the time/increment step number to read/write the first set of data. Time-based values are based upon currently set timescale units timescale units . See also: Solution Options Solution Options

topics.title: Draping Options
topics.text: Draping Options Draping options can be accessed via the Model Properties or Draping options objects in the Analyses Treeview. Draping options can only be specified to be common for all analyses. The draping options control the composite lamina draping process. The draping process works by effectively draping a square mesh of pinned bars over the structure. The length of the bars is considered to be the drape mesh size. A smaller bar size provides a more accurate drape at the expense of computer time and memory usage. Typically the drape mesh size should be about half the element size. Drape by mesh size - Desired drape cell size. (See note below) Drape by number - Desired number of drape cells on draping surface. This must be between the maximum and minimum values stated below. Drape by face multiplier - A number that is used to multiply the actual number of mesh divisions on a draping surface to arrive at a desired drape cell number. This must be between the maximum and minimum values stated below. A default value of 4 is entered. Maximum number of drape cells - Maximum number of drape cells to be generated. Minimum number of drape cells - Minimum number of drape cells to be generated. Extend drape grid one row - Description needed Trim drape grid - Description needed Notes . If the desired drape cell size would generate more than the specified maximum number of drape cells then the drape mesh size would be adjusted to generate the maximum number of drape cells. Likewise, if the desired drape cell size would generate less than the specified minimum number of drape cells then the drape mesh size would be adjusted to generate the minimum number of drape cells. See also: Solution Options Solution Options
topics.search_text: Draping Options Model Properties - Solution Draping Options dlg0prop idd props document solution draping.htm Draping Options Draping options can be accessed via the Model Properties or Draping options objects in the Analyses Treeview. Draping options can only be specified to be common for all analyses. The draping options control the composite lamina draping process. The draping process works by effectively draping a square mesh of pinned bars over the structure. The length of the bars is considered to be the drape mesh size. A smaller bar size provides a more accurate drape at the expense of computer time and memory usage. Typically the drape mesh size should be about half the element size. Drape by mesh size - Desired drape cell size. (See note below) Drape by number - Desired number of drape cells on draping surface. This must be between the maximum and minimum values stated below. Drape by face multiplier - A number that is used to multiply the actual number of mesh divisions on a draping surface to arrive at a desired drape cell number. This must be between the maximum and minimum values stated below. A default value of 4 is entered. Maximum number of drape cells - Maximum number of drape cells to be generated. Minimum number of drape cells - Minimum number of drape cells to be generated. Extend drape grid one row - Description needed Trim drape grid - Description needed Notes . If the desired drape cell size would generate more than the specified maximum number of drape cells then the drape mesh size would be adjusted to generate the maximum number of drape cells. Likewise, if the desired drape cell size would generate less than the specified minimum number of drape cells then the drape mesh size would be adjusted to generate the minimum number of drape cells. See also: Solution Options Solution Options

topics.title: Element Options
topics.text: Element Options Element options are accessed via the Model Properties dialog or the Model Properties control object in the Analyses Treeview. Element options can only be specified to be common for all analyses. See the Element Reference Manual for details of which elements can be used with these options Assign 6 degrees of freedom to all thick shell element thick shell element nodes By default this option is on. It has the effect of adding a rotational spring stiffness to the drilling rotation of the thick shell elements making the analysis more stable. The value of the spring stiffness can be adjusted using the system parameter STFINP. For problems in which geometric nonlinearity (Option 87) is being used more accurate results may be obtained by switching this option off and letting LUSAS automatically establish the need for 5 or 6 degrees of freedom at a node. (LUSAS Solver option 278). Axisymmetric about the global X-axis When selected, LUSAS considers the line of axisymmetry in an analysis to be about the global X axis and not the default, which is the global Y axis. (LUSAS Solver option 47). Lumped mass matrix (structural) Formulate lumped mass matrix instead of consistent mass matrix for elements. (LUSAS Solver option 105). Lumped mass matrix (thermal) Formulate lumped mass matrix instead of consistent mass matrix for elements. (LUSAS Solver option 105). Write strains to output file causes element strains to be written to the Solver output file. Preserve loading whilst elements deactivated retains the loading assigned to all elements in model (activated and deactivated) until a subsequent load case is applied. Typical usage would, for example, be when carrying out a staged construction analysis. Self weight would be assigned to all elements (activated and deactivated) in the loadcase representing stage 1 of the analysis. As stage 2 and subsequent loadcases are activated the loading initially applied to elements in stage 1 would automatically be applied as the elements become active. Note that when using this option no additional loading should be applied to any loadcases following the one that contained the load assignments. If done so, the initial applied loading for those loadcases will be lost. Improved transverse shear for thick shells When selected, and only if equivalent stress is computed, a parabolic distribution of shear stress is calculated, having a mid-shell maximum value of 1.5 x Fy average . Top and bottom shell shears will report as zero. When not checked, constant shear is obtained. Show results for rigid zone elements By default, the elements representing rigid ends of beams do not present element-based results when results are viewed, displayed or printed. By selecting this option these may be obtained. Internal displacements and deformations for beams By default this option is off. When set, it uses the LUSAS Solver calculated deformations at each internal calculation point in each beam element. Residual bending flexibility correction When selected, improves the bending performance of thin shell (TTS3) elements.

topics.title: Integration options
topics.text: Integration options Fine integration for stiffness and mass (structural) Invokes a finer numerical integration rule for elements. (LUSAS Solver option 18). Fine integration for stiffness and mass (thermal) Invokes a finer numerical integration rule for elements. (LUSAS Solver option 18). Fine integration for mass (HX16 and HX20) (HX16 and HX20) Formulate mass matrix with fine integration. (LUSAS Solver option 91). Coarse integration for semi-loof shells semi-loof shells Invokes coarse numerical integration rule for semiloof elements. This option under - integrates the semi - loof shell element which may have the effect of removing low energy mechanisms when the element is very thin and/or pressure loaded. (LUSAS Solver option 19). Newton-Cotes Integration Newton-Cotes Integration for beam elements Newton - Cotes is a form of numerical integration or quadrature. It is often used for through - thickness integrals since sampling points are located at the extremes of the range. (LUSAS Solver option 134). See also: Solution Options Solution Options

topics.title: Geometric nonlinearity
topics.text: Geometric nonlinearity Total Lagrangian A strain formulation that has its reference as the initial configuration at the start of the analysis. (LUSAS Solver option 87). Updated Lagrangian A strain formulation that has its reference as the end of the last converged increment. (LUSAS Solver option 54). Eulerian A strain formulation that has its reference as the current configuration. (LUSAS Solver option 167). Co - rotational Form of geometric nonlinearity in which large displacement effects are related to a set of axes that follow and rotate with the element. (LUSAS Solver option 229). P-Delta An approximate geometrically nonlinear analysis typically used to take account of the interaction between vertical and horizontal (sway) loading on tall, slender buildings, where vertical constant loads (usually dead loads) are used to form a geometric stiffness (stress stiffened) matrix for the structure; additional live load cases can then be applied and load combinations used to capture the effects of the interaction between lateral and vertical loading. (LUSAS Solver option 421). Note that these options are not applicable to thermal analysis. For more information see Geometric Nonlinear Analysis. Geometric Nonlinear Analysis.

topics.title: Solution control
topics.text: Solution control Allows fine control over advanced nonlinear solution procedures. Continue solution after convergence fails This option continues with a nonlinear analysis even after an increment has failed to converge. It is useful for creating a results dump of an unconverged results file to visualise problem areas. This option should be used with care. (LUSAS Solver option 16). Continue solution if more than one negative pivot occurs will step over the LUSAS error that stops the analysis if more than one negative pivot is encountered. This can be useful if pivot problems are encountered at an early stage but the problem is free from them during later stages. This option should be used with care as it is likely to hide more fundamental analysis problems. (LUSAS Solver option 62). Non-symmetric solution (LUSAS Solver option 64). This is set automatically by LUSAS Modeller when, for example, carrying out a nonlinear concrete material modelling of cracking. Carry out an undrained solution For soils modelling, carries out an instantaneous undrained solution. This would be applicable if the loading for a particular soil type is applied such that there is no time for the build up of excess pore water pressures to dissipate. See also: Solution Options Solution Options

topics.title: Display style
topics.text: Display style By default Geometry is viewed in wireframe mode with hidden parts shown, but a wide variety of styles can be obtained by mixing the options for wireframe with and without hidden line and solid plots. By selecting the appropriate check boxes the following can be displayed: Outline only Show only the model outline. Transparent Display colour filled regions with transparency. Wireframe The default display style. All hidden parts are visible Facets and Facets only if selected By default lines and surfaces are assigned a facet density which is used in visualisation. These options display the facets in use. Solid Displays surfaces and volumes in a solid colour. Maximum shade (for solid mesh only) A percentage value that controls how dark a solid mesh colour becomes (with respect to black) when the feature or object on which they are displayed is rotated into the plane of the screen. The default value of 60% darkens a colour by 60% of the difference between the defined colour and black and ensures that meshes drawn on orthogonal surfaces are shaded sufficiently to distinguish the separate sides of the features. Lower values of shade will lessen the difference, higher values increase the difference. Hidden lines (for Wireframe selected only). Include or exclude as appropriate. Internal lines Include or exclude as appropriate.

topics.title: Orientation axes
topics.text: Orientation axes Line directions Displays an arrow to indicate the local x direction of Line. Line axes Displays a local coordinate axis to indicate the local x direction of the line and the orientation of the other axes Combined line directions Displays an arrow to indicate the local x direction of the set of lines defining the Combined Line. Surface axes Displays a local coordinate axis to indicate the orientation of the surface. Surface normals Displays an arrow in the direction of the 'positive' normal for a surface which also shows the orientation of the surface Volume axes Display a local coordinate axis to indicate the orientation of the volume. The origin for the axis is closest to the first point in the first Surface of the Volume definition. Orientations only if selected Display line directions or local coordinate axes only on selected features. Aids with visualisation of geometry orientation on large models. topics.title: Mesh settings
topics.text: Mesh settings Wireframe Displays the element mesh as a wireframe using the pen specified. Only the visible mesh lines are drawn. Transparent Displays a solid filled mesh with a transparency. Solid Displays the mesh as solid panels using the colour specified. Click on the coloured square to change the colour used. Maximum shade (for solid mesh only) A percentage value that controls how dark a solid mesh colour becomes (with respect to black) when the feature or object on which they are displayed is rotated into the plane of the screen. The default value of 60% darkens a colour by 60% of the difference between the defined colour and black and ensures that meshes drawn on orthogonal surfaces are shaded sufficiently to distinguish the separate sides of the features. Lower values of shade will lessen the difference, higher values increase the difference. Hidden edges Displays element edges and not just those of the the visible element faces. Internal edges Displays internal element edges. Show nodes Draws the mesh nodes. Nodes define the vertices of elements. Outline only Displays only the outline of the mesh for each assigned feature. This is also useful for spotting cracks or discontinuities in the mesh due to features not being merged or equivalenced correctly. The Threshold (deg) value controls when edges of elements are drawn. Edges of adjacent elements are drawn when the angle between the normals of adjacent elements exceeds the threshold value. Show normals Displays the element normal for Surface elements Joints offset distance Show element axes Displays the element axes as a local axis set. Orientations only if selected Displays the surface normal or element axes only if the element is selected. % of elements remaining Shrinks the elements to the percentage specified. Colour by Enables the mesh colour to be changed. Mesh colour - colours elements in default mesh colour. Group - colours elements by group. Connectivity - colours element edges by number of neighbours. Element Type - colours elements by element type. Normals - colours elements by surface normal direction. Note. The arrow sizes used for element axes and normals are defined on the Default tab of the Model Properties Model Properties . topics.title: View
topics.text: View Scale to fit window/page When enabled automatically adjusts the zoom level to fit the model to the view window/page. Scale (with Scale to fit window/page disabled) allows the scale ratio of the view to be set manually Origin position Defines the origin of the view. Perspective projection Switches from isometric to perspective viewing of the model. View angle determines the rate at which the perspective distortion occurs. A suggested initial setting is 45. Close depth This parameter determines how far in front of the view position objects are removed from the visualisation. If it is set to zero, an object will grow to infinite size on the screen before it disappears from view. If it is greater than zero, then objects will disappear from view as the depth is reduced. This is input as a percentage of the view depth at 100% zoom, and is defaulted to 1%. Show only activated elements Controls whether only the elements activated in the active loadcase are displayed or not. Border annotation Border annotation Displays an annotated frame containing the LUSAS version number in use with the model name, date, title, and the model units. Summary annotation Summary annotation An automatically assembled text block that displays information about the model such as its view scale and orientation and, if a results file is loaded, a summary of key values and settings for a particular loadcase. Rotation Vector An equivalent eye position coordinate. Entering (0, 0, 1) views the model from the Z axis, and (1, 2, 3) gives a three - dimensional view Rotation increment Sets the rotation increment used for incremental rotation. Location Opens a dialog to allow the location of the summary block of text to be set with reference to the left, right, bottom or top of paper. Note that the Window summary can be moved more easily graphically by selecting it and then dragging it to a new position. Save View Saves the current view settings in a named entry in the Utilities treeview. See Saved views Saved views for more information. See also View Properties View Properties

topics.title: Initial deformations / cable sag
topics.text: Initial deformations / cable sag Exaggerate initial deformations (Off by default) Initial deformations may be inherited from a previous analysis, as for example with an initial imperfection in a girder system generated from an eigenvalue buckling mode, used for a full nonlinear buckling analysis. See Specifying an Initial State for an Analysis Specifying an Initial State for an Analysis for details. In such a case, usually the initial deformation is not exaggerated (displayed at a scale of 1:1), so that it is not distracting when examining deformations in the current (e.g. nonlinear buckling) analysis. However the initial deformation can be exaggerated by turning on this check-box. Note. When displaying deformed mesh plots of contact analyses the exaggeration factor should be set to 1.0 to avoid producing misleading or overlapping results. See also View Properties View Properties Deformed Mesh Plots Deformed Mesh Plots About Results About Results About Loadcases About Loadcases

topics.title: Screen
topics.text: Screen When connecting a laptop or PC to an external screen or projector it is possible to specify which screen should be used to ensure that fonts and other rendered information can be seen at an appropriate resolution. Automatic Contains a dropdown containing an entry for each connected screen for which physical size information can be determined. Selecting an entry and pressing apply will rescale all the objects within LUSAS Modeller to a size appropriate for the selected screen. If no screen sizes can be detected, then the manual field will be selected by default and populated using a screen pixel-based calculation. Manual size Allows a screen size to be specified (measured in inches between diagonal corners of the screen). Note. The setting made applies on a per-session basis. It applies over all active windows and will remain when models are loaded and unloaded. The setting is not saved to the model file or to the registry, so it will reset if LUSAS Modeller is closed and opened again. See also View Properties View Properties Deformed Mesh Plots Deformed Mesh Plots About Results About Results About Loadcases About Loadcases

topics.title: Visualising using the Attribute layer
topics.text: Visualising using the Attribute layer Defined attributes are listed separately for each attribute type. The attributes may be visualised as follows: All / All opaque ('All opaque' for Geometric tab only) Visualises all attributes including any new attributes defined for this attribute type. (Black tick) All transparent (Geometric tab only) Visualises all attributes as transparent. (Grey tick) None Visualises none of the attributes. (No tick) Note that subsequent individual selection of attributes in the right-hand panel will override the button setting made, with repeated selection of the same item cycling through the 'All', 'Transparent' and 'None' options. The From results file option, present for only the Supports and Loading tabs, and only when results are loaded, draws supports and loadings from the results file as opposed to the Model file. In the case of supports there is no difference between the two options. For loadings, when drawn from the results file option, equivalent nodal loads will be drawn as opposed to actual defined loads. The Deform option, present when results are loaded, allows the attributes to be visualised on the deformed mesh. The deformed mesh can be drawn to a Scale dictated by either a specified magnitude (a screen-based value) or a deformation factor (a model-based value).

topics.title: Problems in using Hardware Graphics Drivers
toc_path: Problems in using Hardware Graphics Drivers
headings: Problems in using Hardware Graphics Drivers
topics.text: Problems in using Hardware Graphics Drivers Problems can occasionally be encountered due to the Hardware OpenGL drivers being used to control the graphics display. This will only occur when the LUSAS Hardware OpenGL drivers option is also selected on the LUSAS Configuration Utility. If this happens, you should ensure that your graphic card drivers are the latest stable version as provided by the graphic card's manufacturer. Visit the manufacturer's web site to download any updated drivers and restart Modeller to test. If updating your graphics drivers does not solve the problem you can manually alter the Windows hardware acceleration settings to see if this will prevent the problem from occurring. To do this: Exit Modeller Choose Start > Control Panel > Display > Settings > Advanced > Troubleshoot . Lower the Windows hardware acceleration setting by one step and press the Apply button. Run the LUSAS Configuration Utility LUSAS Configuration Utility and make sure that the Hardware OpenGL drivers option is selected on the Graphics Graphics tab. Restart Modeller and see if any errors related to graphics display problems are still reported. If errors are reported, repeat the whole process from stage 1, lowering the Windows hardware acceleration by another step. If lowering the Windows hardware acceleration settings does not solve the problem, software graphics acceleration will have to be used. Run the LUSAS Configuration Utility LUSAS Configuration Utility and select the Microsoft software OpenGL drivers option on the Graphics Graphics tab to do this.

Run the LUSAS Configuration Utility LUSAS Configuration Utility and select the Microsoft software OpenGL drivers option on the Graphics Graphics tab to do this.

topics.title: Warning - When creating a new loadcase if loading has previously been applied to a range of loadcases
toc_path: Warning - When creating a new loadcase if loading has previously been applied to a range of loadcases
headings: Warning - When creating a new loadcase if loading has previously been applied to a range of loadcases
topics.text: Warning - When creating a new loadcase if loading has previously been applied to a range of loadcases The warning message "Attributes have been assigned to new loadcase <loadcase name> from one or more existing assignments to a range of loadcases" appears if other loadcases present in the Analyses treeview have loading assigned to them specified using the 'range' assignment option on the loading assignment dialog loading assignment dialog Example 1 For a model with four loadcases, called LC1, LC2, LC3, LC4. Using the loading assignment dialog, a load has been assigned with a range from LC1 to LC4. Subsequently adding a new LC5 on to the end does not acquire the load assignment, because the range stops at LC4. However, if LC5 is subsequently moved up the tree, so that it is placed between LC2 and LC3, then LC5 does now acquire the load assignment, because LC5 is now inside the range specified. Example 2 For the same starting model, with four loadcases, called LC1, LC2, LC3, LC4. Using the loading assignment dialog, a load has been assigned with a range 'from' LC1 'to the end of the analysis'. Subsequently adding a new LC5 on to the end does acquire the load assignment, because LC5 is before the end of the analysis. Subsequently dragging LC5 up the tree, so that it is placed between LC2 and LC3, makes no change to the loading because all loadcases are still between LC1 and the end of the analysis. (LC5 is still loaded) Example 3 For the same starting model, with four loadcases, called LC1, LC2, LC3, LC4. Using the loading assignment dialog, a load has been assigned with a range that specifies that the load is assigned to the chosen loadcases LC1 and LC2 and LC3 and LC4. Subsequently adding a new LC5 on to the end does not acquire the load assignment, because LC5 is not in the list of specified loadcases. Subsequently dragging LC5 up the tree, so that it is placed between LC2 and LC3, makes no change to the loading, because LC5 is still not in the list of specified loadcases. (LC5 is still not loaded)

topics.title: Warning - Cannot Find Window
topics.text: Warning - Cannot Find Window LUSAS could not find a window of a specified name. This error probably happened because a window was specified by name from a script, but the window did not exist. For example the following script line will search for a window: call getView("frame2d Window 1").setCurrent() If the window name "Lusas1 Window 1" did not exist in the current model then an error would occur.

topics.title: Warning - Cannot Find Window Number
topics.text: Warning - Cannot Find Window Number LUSAS will try to tackle the above problem by searching for a window of the same name, but with a different end number. LUSAS will issue a warning is this also failed. Typically, this only happens if you has edited the script for example, deleted a window, then tried to set it active.

topics.title: Warning - Cannot Visualise an Attribute
topics.text: Warning - Cannot Visualise an Attribute LUSAS cannot visualise attributes unless the feature is meshed. You will only get this warning if there are no nodes in the model. If some features are meshed, and others are not, the warning will not appear.

topics.title: Units Converter and Variation Utility
topics.text: Units Converter and Variation Utility The Units Converter and Variation Utility dialog can be accessed from all dialogs where dimensional input is expected by clicking inside the right-hand edge of an edit box or grid cell that supports the dimensional input. The dialog can be expanded or contracted according to use by pressing the ' + ' expand or ' - ' contract buttons.. The dialog also adjusts itself according to whether the value in the edit box, or cell, that was used to access it supports units conversion or specification of variations. Each utility is normally used in isolation, however they can be used together if appropriate. Once a units conversion is chosen, the selection persists until changed.

topics.title: Units Converter
topics.text: Units Converter Units can be converted at the time of input on all dialogs where dimensional input is expected by clicking inside the right-hand edge of the edit box or grid cell and accessing the Units Converter and Variation Utility. A range of conversion units are supplied according to the type of input expected. Model units stated are those currently in use. Reporting of expected model units and accessing the Units Convertor dialog For edit boxes or grid cells that support coordinate entry the conversion utility allows conversion of multiple comma separated values in the one text box. So, for instance, a coordinate entered as 100,200,300 would be converted to (0.1, 0.2, 0.3) if a millimetres to metres conversion was selected. Not all values edit box or grid cell values support units conversion. In these cases the Units Converter cannot be expanded.

topics.title: Timescale units
topics.text: Timescale units Timescale units Timescale units can also be converted at the time of input on all dialogs where time-based input is expected by clicking inside the right-hand edge of the edit box or grid cell. For instance, in some modelling situations, such as staged construction modelling of concrete, the age properties are best defined in days rather than seconds. This provides an alternative to modifying the timescale units on the Model properties dialog prior to defining the input.

topics.title: Variations
topics.text: Variations Variations allow parameters in attributes to be varied over the assigned geometry by defining the manner in which the parameter will vary. If a variation is not specified, the parameters within an attribute will be constant over the geometry to which the attribute is assigned. Variations can be defined on all dialogs where dimensional input is expected by clicking inside the right-hand edge of the edit box or grid cell and accessing the Units Converter and Variation Utility. Not all values edit box or grid cell values support variations. In these cases the Variations Utility cannot be expanded. See also: Modelling Units Modelling Units Variations Variations

The following options are also available: Show Tooltips shows a temporary description of the toolbar button when the cursor is moved over the button. topics.title: Customizing toolbar groups
topics.text: Customizing toolbar groups Toolbar buttons can be added to exiting toolbar groups or placed on new toolbar button groups. Use the Customize tab to select a toolbar category and then, from the arrangement of buttons shown for that category, drag and drop a toolbar button into an empty part of the user interface. This can be repeated for as many buttons are necessary. As each button is added the button group will enlarge to accommodate it. Button groups can be 'docked ' alongside other button groups on the user interface by dragging and dropping into place. Buttons may be removed from toolbar groups by holding down the Alt key and then dragging the button into the View window. See also: Toolbars Toolbars

topics.title: Creating a new toolbar group
topics.text: Creating a new toolbar group Favourite toolbar buttons (and any user-defined toolbar buttons) can be grouped together into a new toolbar group. Use the New button on the Toolbars dialog to create a new, named toolbar group such as 'Personal'. An empty 'Personal' button group will be added to the Modeller user interface. Use the Customise tab to select a toolbar category and then, from the arrangement of buttons shown for that category, drag and drop a toolbar button into the 'Personal' button group region of the user interface. This can be repeated for as many buttons are necessary. As each button is added the button group will enlarge to accommodate it. Button groups can be 'docked ' alongside other button groups on the user interface by dragging and dropping into place. See also: Toolbars Toolbars

topics.title: Creating user-defined toolbar button actions
topics.text: Creating user-defined toolbar button actions Nine user-definable toolbar buttons are provided for linking to a specified action. With the Customize tab selected these can be seen if the User entry is selected in the Categories list. Scripts can be recorded and specified to be played when a particular user-defined toolbar button is selected. In Modeller, use File > Script > Start Recording to record an action to be taken (such as the adding a Contours layer to the Treeview and the selecting a particular entity such as Force / Moment, and a component such as Mz, for example). Then use File > Script Stop Recording to save the script with a name such as Bending.vbs to a folder. Then use the User tab to define the action that a particular user-defined toolbar button should take when pressed. This involves inserting a text string to reference the script that was recorded. A typical entry would read: Fileopen "C:\LUSAS144\Projects\Bending.vbs" Default numbered user button images are supplied but these can be edited to suit. See changing user-defined toolbar button images changing user-defined toolbar button images for details See also: Toolbars Toolbars

topics.title: Solver System Variables
topics.text: Solver System Variables Making changes to Solver system variables should be done only after seeking advice from LUSAS Technical Support. Solver variables allowing user-defined values are: Variable Description ICNTCT Controls how lift-off freedoms are allowed to lift-off or re-ground in a nonlinear analysis. Values can be 0, 1, 2 or 3) See also MXLFTO. LFRADD Number of blocks of free space stored for use in a disk file LPGNUM Number of pages held in the in-core page table at any time MAXERR Maximum number of times a single error will be output MEIGSH Maximum number of eigen-solutions computed at a shift point MXELGP Maximum number of elements stored in a particular group MXLFTO Limits the number of times in a nonlinear loading increment that the lift-off variables can be released or restored. See also ICNTCT. MXSLAE Maximum number of adjacent elements for contact nodes in slidelines MXSLAN Maximum number of adjacent nodes for contact nodes in slidelines MXWAIT Maximum wait in seconds for DTF file before terminating analysis NIDX The number of entries allowed in the index table NLPZ Number of real locations in workspace NPGS Maximum number of records allowed in the cache PENTLY Penalty stiffness used in constraint equations PVTTOL Pivot tolerance with BCS solver for numerical factorisation of non-positive-definite matrices (e.g. with constraint equations) QTOL Yield function convergence tolerance SLSTAN Tangential slideline stiffness, as a factor of normal stiffness SLSTCC Slideline stiffness coefficient for close contact SLSTFM Maximum ratio of maximum to minimum slideline stiffnesses STEFAN Stefan-Boltzmann constant, the temperature units of the value input must be Kelvin STFIMP In-plane stiffness parameter for flat shell elements STFSCL Factor applied to stiffness matrix of inactive element TOLNOD Tolerance distance for node on node contact in slidelines

topics.title: Create Holes
topics.text: Create Holes Create a hole in a selected Surface from any selected Surfaces and/or closed loops of Lines that are being used to represent holes. Multiple holes can be created in one operation by selecting multiple Surfaces or multiple closed loops of Lines. Delete geometry defining holes controls whether points, lines and surfaces representing holes are re-used or not in the resulting creation of a surface that contains a hole or holes. Checking the Delete geometry defining holes (the default option) deletes the original points, lines and surface(s) that define a hole, creates new points and lines, and uses those as part of the definition of the enclosing surface to represent the boundary representing the hole. Unchecking the Delete geometry defining holes option retains the original points, lines and surface(s) that define a hole and uses those original points and lines as part of the definition of the surface that encloses the existing surface. The original surface is retained. See also: Holes Holes Arbitrary Section Property Calculator Arbitrary Section Property Calculator

headings: Define an Arc/Circle from Points and/or Coordinates
topics.text: Define an Arc/Circle from Points and/or Coordinates Add or edit the coordinates as required so that three coordinates exist. Any selected Points are listed as the point coordinates in the dialog. Indicate which Point is the arc defining Point, as either the Centre , Direction or Bulge point. The diagrams below illustrate the different methods. Notice the difference between specifying a minor and a major arc. Third arc Point position: Bulge P2 is the bulge Point. Centre P3 is the centre Point. (L2 is the major arc.) Direction P3 is the directional Point. A radius is required to define the arc. (P5 defines the major arc). Note that if a radius that is too small is used, LUSAS will display the minimum radius possible. topics.title: Copy Geometry
topics.text: Copy Geometry Copy previously selected geometry (and assignments) to a new position a specified number of times using a transformation. The transformation can be defined on the copy dialog, or previously defined transformations may be specified. Saved transformations can be combined to perform compound transformations. Mirroring of selected features about a plane defined by their right-hand extremity Mirroring of selected features about a selected specified line Either specify a new transformation type: Translate , Rotate , Mirror (screen) , Matrix , Scale , Compound or Mirror (advanced) and enter the required values, or if available, select a previously defined transformation from the list. Refer to Moving and Copying Geometry Moving and Copying Geometry for general information about these options. Detailed information on the Mirror screen option is shown below.

topics.title: Mirror (screen)
topics.text: Mirror (screen) Previously selected geometry can be mirrored either vertically (Top or Bottom) or horizontally (Left or Right) using a mirror plane, which is perpendicular to the screen. The location of the copied selection is defined by one of the four extremities of the selection, or alternatively about a specified line. For the About specified line option the line can be at any orientation. A plane is constructed by projecting this specified line normal to the screen plane, and is then used for mirroring. Notes: Items selected for mirroring about the screen axes are represented by black lines on the dialog, with the effect of the mirroring setting chosen being shown in default feature colours, above, below, to the left, or to the right of the selection. The mirror (screen) option is only available when the screen is aligned with one of the model axes (i.e. model X, model Y or model Z must be pointing straight out of the screen). The top, left, right and bottom options are only available when the screen is aligned with all of model axes (i.e. model X must align with screen X, Y or Z, and similarly for model Y and model Z). If only a single line, and also some surfaces or volumes are selected, the selected line is used as the 'About specified line' for the mirroring operation. If a line or lines are put into selection memory, these line numbers will appear in the 'About specified line' droplist in preference to any selected on screen. If a gap is required between the geometry selected and the mirrored geometry to be created, a line at the mirror plane must either exist, or be defined, and be selected. If it is required to overlap the geometry selected and the geometry to be created, the 'Mirror (advanced)' option must be used.

headings: Define an Elliptical arc/ Ellipse from Coordinates
topics.text: Define an Elliptical arc/ Ellipse from Coordinates An ellipse, or a length of elliptical arc can be created from entered coordinates, or by pre-selection of suitable drawn points that may be used to define basic ellipse point data. Ellipse point coordinates and settings are used to define the arc/ellipse in the following ways: Start Point, Centre Point and End Point Defines an arc between the start and end coordinates, with the other specified coordinate defining the centre of the ellipse about which the arc is generated.. In Plane (only seen when defining an ellipse) is a point (which does not have to be on the circumference of the ellipse) that will define the plane in which the ellipse is drawn from the defined centre, and start and end point of the arc defining the ellipse. The Axis direction is specified by selecting either a Major axis or Minor axis along with stating an x, y, z direction vector to define the direction from the centre in which the major or minor axis resides. For example entering values of '0 1 0' would define an axis in the Y direction. Minor part , Major part or Full ellipse options draw either an elliptical arc of the shortest length between the start and end points, an arc of the longest length between two points, or a full ellipse based upon all the associated data.

headings: Define Points by Intersecting Lines - Advanced
topics.text: Define Points by Intersecting Lines - Advanced These options define how points can be created when selected lines don't directly intersect each other. All point pairs Creates points along one selected line and corresponding pairs of points along the other selected line according to the types of lines selected. For a spline and a line pairs of points will be created for all locations where the tangent of the spline has the same unit vector as the line. In the case of two parallel lines the order that the lines are selected will dictate at which ends of the lines a point pair will be created. Nearest point pair only Creates a point on one selected line at the closest location of another selected line. When selected lines overlay each other and intersect visually in, say, a plan view (without intersecting directly), a line connecting the two points created will give the shortest distance between the two lines. When the option Allow extended lines is selected a point at the intersection of the two lines will be created. When the option Allow extended lines is not selected, and the lines are not parallel and do not overlay each other visually, no points will be created. Nearest pair to reference position Creates a point on one selected line at the closest location of another selected line that is nearest (of all possible points) to a specified reference coordinate. Limit distance between points Provides a means of filtering or reducing the number of points created by specifying a distance within which the pairs of points on two non-intersecting lines will be created See also: Define Points by Intersecting Lines Define Points by Intersecting Lines Defining Points Defining Points Model Properties Model Properties

topics.text: Move Geometry Moves the selected geometry to a new position using a transformation. Transformation can be defined on the move dialog, or previously defined transformations may be specified. Saved transformations can be combined to perform compound transformations. Either specify a the transformation type: Translation , Rotation , Mirror , Scale , or Rotation by matrix and enter the required values, or if available, select a previously defined transformation from the list. The move type available depends on the items in the selection. Most geometry can be moved by simply updating the point coordinates. Holes however need to be redefined by and copy and delete operation which is carried out automatically. topics.title: Sweep Geometry
topics.text: Sweep Geometry Creates new geometry by sweeping lower order geometry into higher order geometry using a transformation, for example, sweeping a Surface into a Volume, or a Point into a Line. A transformation can be defined on-the-fly, or previously defined ones may be specified. Either specify a type of transformation: Translate , Rotate , Mirror , Scale , or Rotation by matrix and enter the required values, or if available, select a previously defined transformation from the list. Sweep type Rotation transformations (and rotation by matrix) will sweep the selected geometry in a curved path along either a minor arc (the shortest arc distance between two points), a major arc (the longest arc distance between two points) or along a straight line path. A circle may be defined by sweeping a point around a major arc. Order of geometry to create Line, Surface and Volume options are provided. Only feature types of the same or a lower order than the selected feature can be generated. Choosing the 'Line' option when sweeping a Line will create only line features connecting the swept lines to the chosen line. Choosing 'Surface' for the same situation, will additionally create the higher-order parent surface. Transformations generated from memory selection If two or three Points were added to selection memory selection memory before the command was initiated then those can be used to define either a translation (2 Points), rotation matrix (2 or 3 Points) or mirror planes (2 or 3 Points). Choose translation (2 Points only), rotation or mirror from the drop - down list, then click the Use button. The transformation can be altered further if required. Press the Save button to save a transformation with a user-defined or a default LUSAS name. Notes. Compound transformations are not applicable to sweep transformations. When a cylindrical or spherical coordinate set is active only X,Y and Z transformation input is supported. See also: Defining and Using Transformations Defining and Using Transformations
topics.search_text: Sweep Geometry Sweep Geometry Sweep Geometry dlg3geom idd sweep.htm Sweep Geometry Creates new geometry by sweeping lower order geometry into higher order geometry using a transformation, for example, sweeping a Surface into a Volume, or a Point into a Line. A transformation can be defined on-the-fly, or previously defined ones may be specified. Either specify a type of transformation: Translate , Rotate , Mirror , Scale , or Rotation by matrix and enter the required values, or if available, select a previously defined transformation from the list. Sweep type Rotation transformations (and rotation by matrix) will sweep the selected geometry in a curved path along either a minor arc (the shortest arc distance between two points), a major arc (the longest arc distance between two points) or along a straight line path. A circle may be defined by sweeping a point around a major arc. Order of geometry to create Line, Surface and Volume options are provided. Only feature types of the same or a lower order than the selected feature can be generated. Choosing the 'Line' option when sweeping a Line will create only line features connecting the swept lines to the chosen line. Choosing 'Surface' for the same situation, will additionally create the higher-order parent surface. Transformations generated from memory selection If two or three Points were added to selection memory selection memory before the command was initiated then those can be used to define either a translation (2 Points), rotation matrix (2 or 3 Points) or mirror planes (2 or 3 Points). Choose translation (2 Points only), rotation or mirror from the drop - down list, then click the Use button. The transformation can be altered further if required. Press the Save button to save a transformation with a user-defined or a default LUSAS name. Notes. Compound transformations are not applicable to sweep transformations. When a cylindrical or spherical coordinate set is active only X,Y and Z transformation input is supported. See also: Defining and Using Transformations Defining and Using Transformations

headings: Define a Line from a Point Tangent to an Arc(s)
topics.text: Define a Line from a Point Tangent to an Arc(s) Defines a straight Line from a Point tangential to an Arc. Arcs should be co-planar. Multiple straight line tangents will be drawn if LUSAS can create tangent lines that touch both 'sides' of the arc. If only one tangent line is possible this will be drawn. Single straight line tangent would be used if two tangents were possible but only one was to be drawn. In this case a reference coordinate (used to define on which side of the selected arc the tangent line should be drawn) is required. For most situations the multiple straight line tangents option should prove adequate. Split tangent lines Select this option to split the selected Arc at the point of contact by inserting two new Arcs. Delete geometry on splitting Unless specified, the original features will still exist after splitting. Select this option to delete the original features.

topics.text: Define a Line Tangent to two Arcs Defines a Line which is tangent to two Arcs. The new Line can be defined as an outside or inside tangent to the selected arcs. Arcs should be co-planar. For most situations the multiple straight line tangent option should prove to be more useful. In this example, inserting an outside tangent between L1 and L2, would insert the lower tangent line because it has both line ends on both Arcs, whereas the top line only has one end on an Arc. topics.title: Shape Wizard
topics.text: Shape Wizard A number of predefined shapes are available to aid model building. By default the origin of the new shapes will be located at a selected Point. Specifying a negative dimension will change the shape relative to the origin. The Solid option specifies the shape to be defined whilst the Type option defines the highest order feature to be used in the shape definition. By default shapes will be created with a origin at 0,0,0 unless a point is selected in which the selected point will be used as the shape origin. The shape may be orientated using a local coordinate if required. For the cylindrical shape there is an option to create the cylinder with a seam which effectively uses only one surface rather than the default two surfaces to define the shape. topics.title: Add Lamina (Solids and Shells)
topics.text: Add Lamina (Solids and Shells) Adds a lamina to a composite stack for use on a solid and/or shell model. Name is automatically created from the prefix specified on the Solids and Shells dialog. Material is populated from any materials previously added to the Attributes treeview. Thickness is the actual thickness of the lamina. Angle is the angle of each lamina relative to the zero fibre direction. See also: Composites Composites

topics.title: Add Lamina (Draped Solids and Shells)
topics.text: Add Lamina (Draped Solids and Shells) Adds a lamina to the composite stack for draping on a shell and/or solid model Name is automatically created from the prefix specified on the Solids and Shells dialog. Material is populated from any materials previously added to the Attributes treeview. Start direction is populated with a Global option by default and by the names of any local coordinate systems that have been previously added to the Attributes treeview. This is the direction that the drape will aligned to. Start point is the position at which the draping alignment will pass through. One or more points can be selected on the model prior to defining lamina in order to populate this drop-down menu. Alternatively, point numbers can be entered at time of use. Volume fraction is the proportion of the volume of a lamina that is fibre with the remaining portion being the resin. For example, a volume fraction of 1 means 100% fibre and no resin, 0.55 means 55% fibre and 45% resin. Thickness has to defined in different ways according to the type of model that the stack will be assigned to: For a 'mesh-only' model (that is, for a model that has been created by importing a LUSAS datafile) - the actual thickness of each lamina would be entered. For 'geometry models' (where a thickness has been previously defined as part of a geometric property, such as a thickness of a shell, for example or where solid elements represent the thickness of a component) a relative thickness of each lamina with respect to unity would be entered. For example, a lamina thickness of 0.25 would be entered if 4 equal thickness lamina were going to be defined for a specified geometric shell thickness of 4mm. (0.25 x 4 = unity) For solid models that are meshed using tetrahedral elements the actual thickness of each lamina would be entered instead of a relative thickness. Offset - Allows a composite layup to be draped on a drape surface which lies within a component. For this situation, use either Positive or Negative according to the position of drape surface. When the drape surface is on the face of the component the offset should be set to Default. See also: Composites Composites

topics.text: Activate and Deactivate Activation and deactivation enables the modelling of a staged construction or demolition process, whereby selected elements are activated and/or deactivated as the simulation process requires. Activate and Deactivate attributes are defined from the Attributes menu and are assigned to features (or elements in a mesh only model). All elements to be used in the model need to be defined at the start of the analysis. See also: Activate and Deactivate Activate and Deactivate Manipulating Attributes Manipulating Attributes
